title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 50 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 378–390 (Night 50, continuing directly from nights-49), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 50 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. Princess Abrīza tells Sharkān that she is the daughter of the king of the Rūm, Ḥardūb, and why her father and the King of Constantinople have turned against the Muslims; Sharkān takes his leave and rides home, is ambushed by Frankish horsemen, and in the end finds that their leader is Abrīza herself, who has tested him in single combat. The night breaks off as Shahrazad perceives the morning. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْمُوفِيَةُ لِلْخَمْسِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-mūfiyatu li-al-khamsīn
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the completing-one to the fifty,
sentences.i: And when it was the fiftieth night,
sentences.n: الْمُوفِيَةُ is "the one that completes": the night that makes up the full fifty.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِيزَةَ قَالَتْ لِلْبَطْرِيقِ هَذَا رَجُلٌ وَاحِدٌ وَأَنْتُمْ مِائَةٌ وَلَكِنْ إِنْ أَرَدْتُمْ مُصَادَمَتَهُ فَأَظْهِرُوا لَهُ وَاحِدًا بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ لِيَظْهَرَ عِنْدَ الْمَلِكِ مَنْ هُوَ الْبَطَلُ مِنْكُمْ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-malikata Abrīzata qālat li-al-baṭrīqi hādhā rajulun wāḥidun wa-antum miʾatun wa-lākin in aradtum muṣādamatahu fa-aẓhirū lahu wāḥidan baʿda wāḥidin li-yaẓhara ʿinda al-maliki man huwa al-baṭalu minkum
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king, the happy, that the queen Abrīza said to the patrician: This is a man, one, and you are a hundred; but if you want to clash with him, then show-yourselves to him one after one, so that it may appear in the presence of the king who is the hero among you.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Queen Abrīza said to the patrician, "This is one man, and you are a hundred. But if you wish to meet him in combat, show yourselves to him one after another, so that the king may see which of you is the hero."
sentences.n: السَّعِيدُأَنَّ is printed as one word: al-saʿīd ("the fortunate") run together with anna ("that"); we point it as two words glued. The archive gives no space, so we keep none. بَطْرِيق (from Greek patrikios) is a Byzantine patrician or noble commander; the text uses it for the Rūm lords. Queen Abrīza is the same woman the narrative goes on calling "the girl" (al-jāriya).

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْبَطْرِيقُ مَا سُورَةٌ وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ لَقَدْ قُلْتِ الْحَقَّ وَلَكِنْ مَا يَخْرُجُ لَهُ أَوَّلًا غَيْرِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-baṭrīqu mā sūratun wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi la-qad qulti al-ḥaqqa wa-lākin mā yakhruju lahu awwalan ghayrī
sentences.l: And the patrician said: mā sūra [obscure]; and by the right of the Messiah, you have indeed said the truth, but there does not go out to him first other than I.
sentences.i: The patrician said, "By the Messiah, you have spoken the truth; but no one goes out to him first except me."
sentences.n: مَا سُورَةٌ is obscure and may be corrupt (perhaps for ما صورة or ما ضرورة, "what need"); we point it as printed and leave it out of the idiomatic line. وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ, "by the right of the Messiah", is a Christian oath, with وَ as the oath particle. The kasra on قُلْتِ is printed in the edition (the speaker addresses a woman).

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ لَهُ اُصْبُرْ حَتَّى أَذْهَبَ إِلَيْهِ وَأُعَرِّفَهُ بِالْخِطَابِ وَأَنْظُرَ مَا عِنْدَهُ مِنَ الْجَوَابِ فَإِنْ أَجَابَ فَهُوَ الصَّوَابُ وَإِنْ أَبَى فَلَا سَبِيلَ لَكُمْ إِلَيْهِ وَأَكُونَ أَنَا وَمَنْ فِى الدَّيْرِ وَجَوَارِيَّ فِدَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-jāriyatu lahu uṣbur ḥattā adhhaba ilayhi wa-uʿarrifahu bi-al-khiṭābi wa-anẓura mā ʿindahu mina al-jawābi fa-in ajāba fa-huwa al-ṣawābu wa-in abā fa-lā sabīla lakum ilayhi wa-akūna anā wa-man fī al-dayri wa-jawāriyya fidāhu
sentences.l: And the girl said to him: Be patient until I go to him and make-him-know with the address, and see what is with him of the answer. If he answers, then he is the right; and if he refuses, then no way for you to him, and I shall be, I and whoever is in the monastery and my girls, his ransom.
sentences.i: The girl said to him, "Wait until I go to him and speak with him, and see what answer he has. If he answers, that is the right course; and if he refuses, then you have no way to him, and I, and everyone in the monastery, and my maids will be his ransom."
sentences.n: Three rhymes in a row, الْخِطَابِ / الْجَوَابِ / الصَّوَابُ, mark this as rhymed prose. أَكُونَ ... فِدَاهُ means "I will be his ransom", that is, I will give myself for him. The shadda printed on جَوَارِيَّ is kept. فَلَا سَبِيلَ is the "no" of absolute negation, with the noun in the accusative.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَى شَرْكَانَ وَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِمَا كَانَ فَتَبَسَّمَ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّهَا لَمْ تُخْبِرْ أَحَدًا بِأَمْرِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma aqbalat ʿalā Sharkāna wa-akhbaratahu bi-mā kāna fa-tabassama wa-ʿalima annahā lam tukhbir aḥadan bi-amrihi
sentences.l: Then she turned toward Sharkān and informed him of what had been, and he smiled, and knew that she had not informed anyone of his affair.
sentences.i: Then she turned to Sharkān and told him what had happened. He smiled, for he understood that she had told no one about him.
sentences.n: أَقْبَلَ عَلَى is "to turn toward, address". The أ in بِأَمْرِهِ is printed by the edition, so it stays as a full letter.

sentences.t: وَإِنَّمَا شَاعَ خَبَرَةُ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ بِغَيْرِ إِرَادَتِهَا فَرَجَعَ بِاللَّوْمِ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ وَقَالَ كَيْفَ رَمَيْتُ رُوحِي فِي بِلَادِ الرُّومِ
sentences.tr: wa-innamā shāʿa khabaratu ḥattā waṣala ilā al-maliki bi-ghayri irādatihā fa-rajaʿa bi-al-lawmi ʿalā nafsihi wa-qāla kayfa ramaytu rūḥī fī bilādi al-Rūmi
sentences.l: And only that his news spread until it reached the king, without her will; so he returned with the blame upon himself, and said: How have I thrown my soul into the lands of Rūm!
sentences.i: It was only that word of him had spread until it reached the king, against her wishes. So he turned the blame on himself and said, "How could I have thrown myself into the land of the Rūm?"
sentences.n: The edition prints خَبَرَة with a tā' marbūṭa where the sense needs the pronoun ـه: it is a slip for خَبَرُهُ, "his news", and the pointing and transliteration follow the printed letters. رَمَيْتُ رُوحِي, "I threw my soul", means "I put myself at risk"; رُوح is used here like a reflexive pronoun, a Middle Arabic habit. الرُّوم are the Byzantine Greeks.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ لَمَّا سَمِعَ كَلَامَ الْجَارِيَةِ قَالَ لَهَا إِنَّ بُرُوزَهُمْ إِنِيَّ وَاحِدًا بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ إِحْجَافٌ بِهِمْ فَهَلَّا يَبْرُزُونَ لِي عَشَرَةً بَعْدَ عَشَرَةٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu lammā samiʿa kalāma al-jāriyati qāla lahā inna burūzahum iniyya wāḥidan baʿda wāḥidin iḥjāfun bihim fa-hallā yabruzūna lī ʿasharatan baʿda ʿasharatin
sentences.l: Then that he, when he heard the speech of the girl, said to her: Indeed their sallying-out [iniyya] one after one is an injustice to them; so why do they not sally out to me ten after ten?
sentences.i: Then, when he heard the girl's words, he said to her, "It does them wrong to come out to me one by one. Why do they not come out ten at a time?"
sentences.n: إِنِيَّ is printed with a shadda on the yā' and makes no sense where it stands. It is most likely a misprint for إِلَيَّ, "to me", which is how the idiomatic line takes it; we point the printed letters. إِحْجَافٌ is printed with ḥ before j, a transposition of إِجْحَاف, "wronging, injustice", and is pointed as printed. إِحْجَافٌ بِهِمْ means "harm done to them": his point is that they are being wasted one at a time.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْجَارِيَةُ هَذِهِ الشَّطَارَةُ ظُلْمٌ وَإِنَّ كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ لِوَاحِدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu al-jāriyatu hādhihi al-shaṭāratu ẓulmun wa-inna kulla wāḥidin li-wāḥidin
sentences.l: And the girl said to him: This bravado is a wrong, and indeed each one is for one.
sentences.i: The girl said to him, "This bravado is unfair; it must be each man against one."
sentences.n: The last clause is elliptical: كُلَّ وَاحِدٍ لِوَاحِدٍ, "each one for one", means a duel is one against one. الشَّطَارَة is daring or cunning bravado; here the girl says that ten against one would be a wrong.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ وَثَبَ عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ وَسَارَ إِلَى أَنْ أَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَكَانَ مَعَهُ سَيْفُهُ وَآلَةُ حَرْبِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa dhālika al-kalāma thaba ʿalā qadamayhi wa-sāra ilā an aqbala ʿalayhim wa-kāna maʿahu sayfuhu wa-ālatu ḥarbihi
sentences.l: And when he heard that speech he leapt upon his two feet and went until he came toward them; and with him was his sword and the tool-of his war.
sentences.i: When he heard that, he sprang to his feet and went on until he came up to them, with his sword and his war-gear at hand.
sentences.n: The آ in وَآلَةُ is printed by the edition and stays precomposed.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ وَثَبَ الْبَطْرِيقُ عَلَيْهِ وَحَمَلَ عَلَيْهِ فَقَابَلَهُ شَرْكَانُ كَأَنَّهُ الْأَسَدُ وَضَرَبَهُ بِالسَّيْفِ عَلَى عَاتِقِهِ فَخَرَجَ السَّيْفُ يَلْمَعُ مِنْ ظَهْرِهِ وَأَمْعَائِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika thaba al-baṭrīqu ʿalayhi wa-ḥamala ʿalayhi fa-qābalahu Sharkānu ka-annahu al-asadu wa-ḍarabahu bi-al-sayfi ʿalā ʿātiqihi fa-kharaja al-sayfu yalmaʿu min ẓahrihi wa-amʿāʾihi
sentences.l: And at that, the patrician leapt upon him and charged upon him, and Sharkān met him as though he were the lion, and struck him with the sword upon his shoulder, and the sword came out gleaming from his back and his bowels.
sentences.i: At that the patrician sprang at him and charged, but Sharkān met him like a lion and struck him on the shoulder with his sword, so that the blade came out gleaming through his back and his entrails.
sentences.n: حَمَلَ عَلَى is "to charge at". يَلْمَعُ, "gleaming", is a present verb used as a circumstantial clause describing the sword as it came out. This stock picture of a sword passing out through the back recurs in the next fights.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ ذَلِكَ عَظُمَ قَدْرُ شَرْكَانَ عِنْدَهَا وَعَرَفَتْ أَنَّهَا حِينَ صَرَعَتْهُ مَا صَرَعَتْهُ بِقُوَّتِهَا بَلْ بِحُسْنِهَا وَجَمَالِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarati al-jāriyatu dhālika ʿaẓuma qadru Sharkāna ʿindahā wa-ʿarafat annahā ḥīna ṣaraʿathu mā ṣaraʿathu bi-quwwatihā bal bi-ḥusnihā wa-jamālihā
sentences.l: And when the girl saw that, the worth of Sharkān grew great with her, and she knew that when she felled him she had not felled him by her strength, but by her beauty and her loveliness.
sentences.i: When the girl saw this, her esteem for Sharkān grew great, and she understood that when she had brought him down earlier it had been by her beauty and charm, not by her strength.
sentences.n: Her "felling" of Sharkān refers back to how she overcame him earlier in the story; the point is that he is a real fighter and she won him by charm, not force. عِنْدَهَا, "with her", means "in her eyes".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَى الْبَطَارِقَةِ وَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ خُذُوا بِثَأْرِ صَاحِبِكُمْ فَخَرَجَ لَهُ أَخُ الْمَقْتُولِ وَكَانَ جَبَّارًا عَنِيدًا فَحَمَلَ عَلَى شَرْكَانَ فَلَمْ يُمْهِلْهُ دُونَ أَنْ ضَرَبَهُ بِالسَّيْفِ عَلَى عَاتِقِهِ فَخَرَجَ السَّيْفُ يَلْمَعُ مِنْ أَمْعَائِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-jāriyata aqbalat ʿalā al-baṭāriqati wa-qālat lahum khudhū bi-thaʾri ṣāḥibikum fa-kharaja lahu akhu al-maqtūli wa-kāna jabbāran ʿanīdan fa-ḥamala ʿalā Sharkāna fa-lam yumhilhu dūna an ḍarabahu bi-al-sayfi ʿalā ʿātiqihi fa-kharaja al-sayfu yalmaʿu min amʿāʾihi
sentences.l: Then that the girl turned toward the patricians and said to them: Take the revenge-of your companion; and there went out to him the brother of the slain, and he was a tyrant, stubborn, and he charged upon Sharkān, and did not give him respite before he struck him with the sword upon his shoulder, and the sword came out gleaming from his bowels.
sentences.i: Then the girl turned to the patricians and said, "Avenge your comrade!" The dead man's brother came out against him, a stubborn brute, and charged Sharkān; but Sharkān gave him no time, and struck him on the shoulder with his sword, and the blade came out gleaming from his entrails.
sentences.n: أَخَذَ بِثَأْرِ is the idiom for taking vengeance (the verb chooses بِـ). The ث with precomposed أ in ثَأْرِ is as the edition prints it. فَلَمْ يُمْهِلْهُ دُونَ أَنْ means he gave him no respite before striking: it was immediate.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ نَادَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ يَا عِبَادَ الْمَسِيحِ خُذُوا بِثَأْرِ صَاحِبِكُمْ فَلَمْ يَزَالُوا يَبْرُزُونَ إِلَيْهِ وَاحِدًا بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ وَشَرْكَانُ يَلْعَبُ فِيهِمْ بِسَيْفِهِ حَتَّى قَتَلَ مِنْهُمْ خَمْسِينَ بَطْرِيقًا وَالْجَارِيَةُ تَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهِمْ وَقَدْ قَذَفَ اللَّهُ الرُّعْبَ فِي قُلُوبِ مَنْ بَقِيَ مِنْهُمْ وَقَدْ تَأَخَّرُوا عَنِ الْبَرَازِ فَلَمْ يَجْسُرُوا عَلَى الْبُرُوزِ إِلَيْهِ بَلْ حَمَلُوا عَلَيْهِ بِأَجْمَعِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika nādati al-jāriyatu yā ʿibāda al-masīḥi khudhū bi-thaʾri ṣāḥibikum fa-lam yazālū yabruzūna ilayhi wāḥidan baʿda wāḥidin wa-Sharkānu yalʿabu fīhim bi-sayfihi ḥattā qatala minhum khamsīna baṭrīqan wa-al-jāriyatu tanẓuru ilayhim wa-qad qadhafa Allāhu al-ruʿba fī qulūbi man baqiya minhum wa-qad taʾakhkharū ʿani al-barāzi fa-lam yajsurū ʿalā al-burūzi ilayhi bal ḥamalū ʿalayhi bi-ajmaʿihim
sentences.l: And at that the girl called out: O worshippers of the Messiah, take the revenge-of your companion! And they did not cease sallying out to him one after one, while Sharkān played among them with his sword, until he killed of them fifty patricians, and the girl looking at them, and God had cast the terror into the hearts of whoever remained of them, and they had held back from the duel, and did not dare to sally out to him; rather they charged upon him with all-of-them.
sentences.i: At that the girl cried, "O servants of the Messiah, avenge your comrade!" And they kept coming out to him one after another, while Sharkān played among them with his sword, until he had killed fifty patricians. The girl watched them, and God had cast terror into the hearts of those who were left, so that they hung back from single combat and no longer dared to come out to him; instead they charged at him all together.
sentences.n: فَلَمْ يَزَالُوا plus a present verb means "they kept on doing". يَلْعَبُ, "plays", is the stock verb for a master swordsman making light work of his enemies. Note that the girl is again the one who rallies the Rūm against Sharkān, as part of her test of him.

sentences.t: وَحَمَلَ هُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِقَلْبٍ أَقْوَى مِنَ الْحَجَرِ إِلَى أَنْ طَحَنَهُمْ طَحْنَ الدِّرَاسِ وَسَلَبَ مِنْهُمُ الْعُقُولَ وَالنُّفُوسَ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥamala huwa ʿalayhim bi-qalbin aqwā mina al-ḥajari ilā an ṭaḥanahum ṭaḥna al-dirāsi wa-salaba minhumu al-ʿuqūla wa-al-nufūsa
sentences.l: And he charged, he, upon them with a heart stronger than the stone, until he ground them the grinding of the threshing, and stripped from them the minds and the souls.
sentences.i: He charged them with a heart harder than stone, until he had ground them down as threshing grinds the grain, and stripped them of their wits and their lives.
sentences.n: طَحْنَ الدِّرَاسِ is "the grinding of the threshing", a cognate accusative of manner: they were ground like grain on the threshing-floor. We point الدِّرَاس as dirās, "threshing"; the printed word is unpointed and could also be read as a different noun, so take this as our best reading.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ عَلَى جَوَارِبِهَا وَقَالَتْ لَهُنَّ مَنْ بَقِيَ فِى الدَّيْرِ فَقُلْنَ لَهَا مَا بَقِيَ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا الْبَوَّابِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥati al-jāriyatu ʿalā jawāribihā wa-qālat lahunna man baqiya fī al-dayri fa-qulna lahā mā baqiya aḥadun illā al-bawwābīna
sentences.l: And the girl shouted at her girls and said to them: Who remains in the monastery? And they said to her: There remains no one except the doorkeepers.
sentences.i: The girl called to her maids and asked them, "Who is left in the monastery?" They answered, "No one is left but the doorkeepers."
sentences.n: جَوَارِبِهَا is printed with a bā' where the sense needs a yā': it is a slip for جَوَارِيهَا, "her girls" (جَوَارِب would mean "stockings"). We point the printed letters. الْبَوَّابِينَ is in the oblique case where Classical would write the nominative after مَا بَقِيَ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا; this is a common Middle Arabic habit, and we point it as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ لَاقَتْهُ وَأَخَذَتْهُ بِالْأَحْضَانِ وَطَلَعَ شَرْكَانُ مَعَهَا إِلَى الْقَصْرِ بَعْدَ فَرَاغِهِ مِنَ الْمُعَارَكَةِ وَكَانَ قَدْ بَقِيَ مِنْهُمْ قَلِيلٌ كَامِنٌ لَهُ فِي زَوَايَا الدَّيْرِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malikata lāqathu wa-akhadhathu bi-al-aḥḍāni wa-ṭalaʿa Sharkānu maʿahā ilā al-qaṣri baʿda farāghihi mina al-muʿārakati wa-kāna qad baqiya minhum qalīlun kāminun lahu fī zawāyā al-dayri
sentences.l: Then that the queen met him and took him in the embraces, and Sharkān went up with her to the palace after his finishing from the fighting; and there had remained of them a few, lurking for him in the corners of the monastery.
sentences.i: Then the queen met him and took him in her arms, and Sharkān went up with her to the palace when the fighting was done. But a few of them were still left, lying in wait for him in the corners of the monastery.
sentences.n: The text calls her "the queen" here and "the girl" elsewhere; she is the same person throughout. أَخَذَتْهُ بِالْأَحْضَانِ is "she took him in embraces" (أَحْضَان, plural of حِضْن, "bosom").

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتِ الْجَارِيَةُ إِلَى ذَلِكَ الْقَلِيلِ قَامَتْ مِنْ عِنْدِ شَرْكَانَ ثُمَّ عَادَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَعَلَيْهَا زَرَدِيَّةٌ ضَيِّقَةُ الْعُيُونِ وَبِيَدِهَا صَارِمٌ هِنْدِيٌّ وَقَالَتْ وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ لَمْ أَبْخَلْ بِنَفْسِي عَنْ ضَيْفِي وَلَا أَتَخَلَّى عَنْهُ وَلَوْا بَقِى بِسَبَبِ ذَلِكَ مَعِيرَةٌ فِي بِلَادِ الرُّومِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarati al-jāriyatu ilā dhālika al-qalīli qāmat min ʿindi Sharkāna thumma ʿādat ilayhi wa-ʿalayhā zaradiyyatun ḍayyiqatu al-ʿuyūni wa-bi-yadihā ṣārimun hindiyyun wa-qālat wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi lam abkhal bi-nafsī ʿan ḍayfī wa-lā atakhallā ʿanhu wa-lawā baqiya bi-sababi dhālika maʿīratun fī bilādi al-Rūmi
sentences.l: And when the girl looked at that few, she rose from beside Sharkān, then returned to him with upon her a coat of mail, narrow-of the eyes, and in her hand an Indian sword; and she said: By the right of the Messiah, I will not be stingy with myself toward my guest, nor abandon him, even if there should remain, because of that, a reproach in the lands of Rūm.
sentences.i: When the girl saw those few, she rose from Sharkān's side and came back to him wearing a close-meshed coat of mail, with an Indian blade in her hand. She said, "By the Messiah, I will not hold myself back from my guest, nor desert him, even if a reproach should remain in the lands of the Rūm because of it."
sentences.n: ضَيِّقَةُ الْعُيُونِ, "narrow of eyes", describes mail whose rings are close-set, the eyes being the links. وَلَوْا is printed with a stray alif after law ("even if"); we point it as وَلَوْ with the alif left silent. مَعِيرَة is an uncommon word for a reproach or disgrace (compare عَيَّرَ, "to reproach"); we take it so, though the printed form may be a variant of مَعَرَّة. بَخِلَ بِنَفْسِهِ عَنْ means "to hold oneself back from".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَأَمَّلَتِ الْبَطَارِقَةَ وَجَدَتْهُ قَتَلَ مِنْهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ وَاِنْهَزَمَ مِنْهُمْ عِشْرُونَ فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتْ إِلَى مَا صَنَعَ بِالْقَوْمِ قَالَتْ لَهُ بِمِثْلِكَ تَفْتَخِرُ الْفُرْسَانُ فَلِلَّهِ دَرُّكَ يَاشَرْكَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā taʾammalati al-baṭāriqata wajadathu qatala minhum thamānīna wa-inhazama minhum ʿishrūna fa-lammā naẓarat ilā mā ṣanaʿa bi-al-qawmi qālat lahu bi-mithlika taftakhiru al-fursānu fa-li-Allāhi darruka yā Sharkānu
sentences.l: And when she scanned the patricians she found that he had killed of them eighty, and there had fled of them twenty. And when she looked at what he had done to the people, she said to him: In the like of you the horsemen take pride; so to God be your milk, O Sharkān!
sentences.i: When she surveyed the patricians she found that he had killed eighty of them and that twenty had fled. And seeing what he had done to the host, she said to him, "Knights take pride in a man like you. God bless your deeds, Sharkān!"
sentences.n: فَلِلَّهِ دَرُّكَ, literally "to God be your milk", is a stock cry of admiration: "what a marvel you are!" It is printed together with the vocative as يَاشَرْكَانُ, and we keep it joined. The verb in تَفْتَخِرُ الْفُرْسَانُ comes before its plural subject and stays singular, as Arabic usually does.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَامَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ يَمْسَحُ سَيْفَهُ مِنْ دَمِ الْقَتْلَى وَيُنْشِدُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu qāma baʿda dhālika yamsaḥu sayfahu min dami al-qatlā wa-yunshidu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: Then that he rose after that, wiping his sword from the blood of the slain and reciting these verses.
sentences.i: Then he stood up and wiped his sword clean of the blood of the slain, and recited these verses.
sentences.n: The verses announced here open the next section of the night. يَمْسَحُ and يُنْشِدُ are present verbs describing what he was doing as he stood.

sentences.t:
وَكَمْ فَرَّقْتُ فِي الْهَيْجَاءِ جَمْعًا * تَرَكْتُ كُمَاتَهُمْ طُعْمَ السِّبَاعِ
سَلُوا عَنِّي وَعَنْهُمْ فِي نِزَالِي * جَمِيعَ الْخَلْقِ فِي يَوْمِ الْقِرَاعِ
تَرَكْتُ لُيُوثَهُمْ فِي الْحَرْبِ صَرْعَى * عَلَى الرَّمْضَاءِ فِي تِلْكَ الْبِقَاعِ
sentences.tr:
wa-kam farraqtu fī al-hayjāʾi jamʿan * taraktu kumātahum ṭuʿma al-sibāʿi
salū ʿannī wa-ʿanhum fī nizālī * jamīʿa al-khalqi fī yawmi al-qirāʿi
taraktu luyūthahum fī al-ḥarbi ṣarʿā * ʿalā al-ramḍāʾi fī tilka al-biqāʿi
sentences.l:
And how many a host I have scattered in the battle: * I left their armoured champions food of the beasts.
Ask, about me and about them, in my fighting, * all of creation, on the day of the clash.
I left their lions in the war laid-low * upon the scorching ground in those tracts.
sentences.i: How many a host I have scattered in battle, leaving their armoured champions as meat for the beasts! Ask all creation about me and about them, and how I fought on the day of the clash. I left their lions stretched out in the war, on the burning ground of those plains.
sentences.n: These are the verses Sharkān recites as he wipes his sword; the next unit says he has finished his verse. The rhyme is -āʿi. كُمَاة (plural of كَمِيّ) are fully armed warriors; صَرْعَى is the plural of صَرِيع, "one thrown down"; الرَّمْضَاء is ground scorched by the sun.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ انْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْجَارِيَةُ مُتَبَسِّمَةً وَقَبَّلَتْ يَدَهُ وَقَلَعَتِ الزَّرَدَ الَّذِي كَانَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi inbalat ʿalayhi al-jāriyatu mutabassimatan wa-qabbalat yadahu wa-qalaʿati al-zarada alladhī kāna ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And when he finished from his poetry, [inbalat] upon him the girl, smiling, and she kissed his hand and pulled-off the mail which was upon her.
sentences.i: When he had finished his poem, the girl came toward him smiling, kissed his hand, and took off the coat of mail she had been wearing.
sentences.n: This sentence continues the scene from the previous line (the girl is Abrīza, in armour). انْبَلَتْ is printed so and is not a word we can place; it is very probably a misprint for أَقْبَلَتْ "she advanced" (the letters ق and ن are close in this type), which is how the idiomatic line reads it. We point it as printed. الزَّرَد is mail, linked rings.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا يَا مَوْلَاتِي لِأَيِّ شَيٌ لَبِسْتِ هَذَا الزَّرَدَ وَشَهَرْتِ حُسَامَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā yā mawlātī li-ayyi shayʾun labistī hādhā al-zarada wa-shahartī ḥusāmaki
sentences.l: And he said to her: O my mistress, for what thing did you put-on this mail and unsheathe your sword?
sentences.i: He said to her, "My lady, why did you put on this mail and draw your sword?"
sentences.n: شَيٌ is printed with a tanwīn on the ي and no hamza: it stands for شَيْء, "thing". After أَيّ it should be genitive (شَيْءٍ), but the print has damma-tanwīn, so we point what is there. The verbs address a woman: لَبِسْتِ, شَهَرْتِ, حُسَامَكِ.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ حِرْصًا عَلَيْكَ مِنْ هُولَاءِ اللِّئَامِ
sentences.tr: qālat ḥirṣan ʿalayka min hāʾulāʾi al-liʾāmi
sentences.l: She said: Eagerness upon you, from these base-ones.
sentences.i: She said, "I was anxious for you, because of these scoundrels."
sentences.n: حِرْصًا عَلَيْكَ is an accusative of purpose: "out of care for you". هُولاء is the demonstrative هؤلاء "these", printed with a plain و and no hamza (the edition has a damma on the first letter, which we keep); read it hāʾulāʾi. اللِّئَام are the base, ignoble men, here the doorkeepers who let the king's men in.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْجَارِيَةَ دَعَتِ الْبَوَّابِينَ وَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ كَيْفَ تَرَكْتُمْ أَصْحَابَ الْمَلِكِ يَدْخُلُونَ مَنْزِلِي بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِي
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-jāriyata daʿat al-bawwābīna wa-qālat lahum kayfa taraktum aṣḥāba al-maliki yadkhulūna manzilī bi-ghayri idhnī
sentences.l: Then that the girl called the doorkeepers and said to them: How did you leave the companions-of the king entering my house without my permission?
sentences.i: Then the girl summoned the doorkeepers and said to them, "How could you let the king's men walk into my house without my leave?"
sentences.n: ثُمَّ إِنَّ is the stock "then" of narrative, as in Night 49. تَرَكْتُمْ ... يَدْخُلُونَ "you left them entering" means "you let them enter". The girl is called الْجَارِيَة throughout, though she is the mistress of the house; Abrīza is a princess.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهَا أَيَّتُهَا الْمَلِكَةُ مَا جَرَتِ الْعَادَةُ أَنَّنَا نَحْتَاجُ إِلَى اسْتِيذَانٍ مِنْكِ عَلَى رُسُلِ الْمَلِكِ خُصُوصًا الْبِطْرِيقَ الْكَبِيرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahā ayyatuhā al-malikatu mā jarati al-ʿādatu annanā naḥtāju ilā istīdhānin minki ʿalā rusuli al-maliki khuṣūṣan al-biṭrīqa al-kabīra
sentences.l: And they said to her: O queen, the custom has not run that we need permission-seeking from you for the messengers of the king, especially the great patrician.
sentences.i: They said to her, "Your Majesty, it has never been our custom to ask your leave for the king's envoys, least of all the Chief Patrician."
sentences.n: اسْتِيذَان is printed for اسْتِئْذَان "asking leave", without the hamza (a common spelling). مَا جَرَتِ الْعَادَةُ أَنَّ ... is a set phrase, "it has not been the custom that ...". الْبِطْرِيق is the Byzantine patrician (from Greek patrikios), a high officer; the plural بَطَارِقَة appears below.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ أَظُنُّكُمْ مَا أَرَدْتُمْ إِلَّا هَتْكِي وَقَتْلَ ضَيْفِي
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahum aẓunnukum mā aradtum illā hatkī wa-qatla ḍayfī
sentences.l: And she said to them: I think you wanted nothing but my tearing-of-the-veil and the killing of my guest.
sentences.i: She said to them, "I think you wanted nothing but to dishonour me and kill my guest."
sentences.n: هَتْك is literally "tearing" (of a veil or covering), hence exposure and disgrace; here, the dishonour of the mistress of the house.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَمَرَتْ شَرْكَانَ أَنْ يَضْرِبَ رِقَابَهُمْ فَضَرَبَ رِقَابَهُمْ وَقَالَتْ لِبَاقِي خُدَّامِهَا إِنَّهُمْ يَسْتَحِقُّونَ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma amarat Sharkāna an yaḍriba riqābahum fa-ḍaraba riqābahum wa-qālat li-bāqī khuddāmihā innahum yastaḥiqqūna akthara min dhālika
sentences.l: Then she commanded Sharkān that he strike their necks, and he struck their necks; and she said to the rest-of her servants: They deserve more than that.
sentences.i: Then she ordered Sharkān to strike off their heads, and he struck off their heads. She said to the rest of her servants, "They deserve worse than that."
sentences.n: ضَرَبَ الرِّقَابَ, "to strike the necks", is the ordinary idiom for beheading, so the idiomatic line says so. Her servants are told that the doorkeepers deserved more than death, a warning to the rest.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ الْتَفَتَتْ إِلَى شَرْكَانَ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ الْآنَ ظَهَرَ لَكَ مَا كَانَ خَافِيًا
sentences.tr: thumma iltafatat ilā Sharkāna wa-qālat lahu al-āna ẓahara laka mā kāna khāfiyan
sentences.l: Then she turned to Sharkān and said to him: Now has appeared to you what was hidden.
sentences.i: Then she turned to Sharkān and said, "Now what was hidden has become plain to you."

sentences.t: فَهَا أَنَا أُعْلِمُكَ بِقِصَّتِي اعْلَمْ أَنِّي بِنْتُ مَلِكِ الرُّومِ حَرْدُوبَ وَاسْمِي أَبْرِيزَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-hā anā uʿlimuka bi-qiṣṣatī iʿlam annī bintu maliki al-Rūmi Ḥardūba wa-ismī Abrīzatu
sentences.l: So here I [am] informing-you of my story: know that I [am] the daughter-of the king-of the Rūm, Ḥardūb, and my name [is] Abrīza.
sentences.i: Now I will tell you my story. Know that I am the daughter of Ḥardūb, king of Rūm, and my name is Abrīza.
sentences.n: اعْلَمْ أَنَّ "know that ..." is a standard way of opening a statement. حَرْدُوب is a foreign name and so takes no tanwīn; it is in apposition to مَلِك, hence the fatḥa as a genitive. أَعْلَمَ بِـ means "to inform of".

sentences.t: وَالْعَجُوزُ الَّتِي تُسَمَّى ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي جَدَّتِي أُمُّ أَبِي وَهِيَ الَّتِي أَعْلَمَتْ أَبِي بِكَ وَلَا بُدَّأَنَّهَا تَعْمَلُ حِيلَةً عَلَى هَلَاكِي سِيَّمَا وَقَدْ قَتَلْتُ بَطَارِقَةَ أَبِي وَشَاعَ أَنِّي قَدِ انْفَرَدْتُ وَتَخَرَّبْتُ مَعَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-al-ʿajūzu allatī tusammā Dhātu al-Dawāhī jaddatī ummu abī wa-hiya allatī aʿlamat abī bika wa-lā budda annahā taʿmalu ḥīlatan ʿalā halākī siyyamā wa-qad qataltu baṭāriqata abī wa-shāʿa annī qad infaradtu wa-takharrabtu maʿa al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And the old-woman who is called Dhāt al-Dawāhī [is] my grandmother, the mother-of my father, and she is the one who informed my father of you; and there is no escape that she will work a stratagem for my destruction, especially as I have killed my father's patricians, and it has spread that I have gone off-alone and [takharrabtu] with the Muslims.
sentences.i: The old woman called Dhāt al-Dawāhī is my grandmother, my father's mother, and it was she who told my father about you. She is certain to scheme my ruin, above all since I have killed my father's patricians and word has spread that I have broken away and thrown in my lot with the Muslims.
sentences.n: Dhāt al-Dawāhī, "Mistress of Calamities", is a name, so it stays nominative as the second term after the passive تُسَمَّى. وَلَا بُدَّأَنَّهَا is printed as one word: wa-lā budda + annahā, "and there is no escaping that she ...". سِيَّمَا is "especially". تَخَرَّبْتُ is not a word we can place with confidence: taken as printed it means "I was ruined", but the sense wanted is "I sided with the Muslims", and the printer may have set تَخَرَّبْتُ for تَحَزَّبْتُ ("I took sides"). We point it as printed and translate by the likely sense.

sentences.t: فَالرَّأْيُ السَّدِيدُ أَنَّنِي أَتْرُكُ الْإِقَامَةَ هُنَا مَا دَامَتْ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي خَلْفِي
sentences.tr: fa-al-raʾyu al-sadīdu annanī atruku al-iqāmata hunā mā dāmat Dhātu al-Dawāhī khalfī
sentences.l: So the opinion, the sound-one, [is] that I leave the staying here as long as Dhāt al-Dawāhī [is] behind me.
sentences.i: So the wise course is for me to give up staying here, so long as Dhāt al-Dawāhī is at my back.
sentences.n: مَا دَامَ "as long as (it) lasts" is the usual way to say "so long as"; it takes a nominative subject and a predicate, here خَلْفِي "behind me".

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ أُرِيدُ مِنْكَ مِثْلَ مَا فَعَلْتُ مَعَكَ مِنَ الْجَمِيلِ لِ تَفْعَلَ مَعِي فَإِنَّ الْعَدَاوَةَ قَدْ وَقَعَتْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ أَبِي مِنْ أَجْلِكَ فَلَا تَتْرُكْ مِنْ كَلَامِي شَيْئًا فَإِنَّ هَذَا كُلَّهُ مَا وَقَعَ إِلَّا مِنْ شَأْنِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin urīdu minka mithla mā faʿaltu maʿaka mina al-jamīli li tafʿala maʿī fa-inna al-ʿadāwata qad waqaʿat baynī wa-bayna abī min ajlika fa-lā tatruk min kalāmī shayʾan fa-inna hādhā kullahu mā waqaʿa illā min shaʾnika
sentences.l: But I want from you the like of what I did with you of the kindness, that you do with me; for enmity has fallen between me and my father on-account-of you; so do not leave anything of my speech, for all of this has not happened except from your affair.
sentences.i: But I ask of you the like of the kindness I showed you, that you may show it to me. Enmity has fallen between me and my father because of you, so do not let any of my words pass unheeded: none of this has happened except on your account.
sentences.n: The printed text divides لِتَفْعَلَ into two words, لِ and تَفْعَلَ; we keep them apart, and the لِ is the one that introduces the purpose clause ("so that you do"). مِنَ الْجَمِيلِ "of the kindness" explains مَا فَعَلْتُ. مِنْ شَأْنِكَ, literally "from your affair", means "on your account".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ طَارَ عَقْلُهُ مِنَ الْفَرَحِ وَاتَّسَعَ صَدْرُهُ وَانْشَرَحَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Sharkānu hādhā al-kalāma ṭāra ʿaqluhu mina al-faraḥi wa-ittasaʿa ṣadruhu wa-insharaḥa
sentences.l: And when Sharkān heard this speech, his mind flew from the joy, and his chest widened and opened-out.
sentences.i: When Sharkān heard this, his wits flew from sheer joy, and his heart swelled and lightened.
sentences.n: Two stock idioms of gladness: طَارَ عَقْلُهُ, "his mind flew", is to be beside oneself with joy, and اتَّسَعَ صَدْرُهُ وَانْشَرَحَ, "his chest widened and opened", is to feel the heart relieved and glad.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَا يَصِلُ إِلَيْكِ أَحَدٌ مَا دَامَ فِي صَدْرِي رُوحٌ وَلَكِنْ هَلْ لَكِ صَبْرٌ عَلَى فِرَاقِ وَالِدِكِ وَأَهْلِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla wa-Allāhi lā yaṣilu ilayki aḥadun mā dāma fī ṣadrī rūḥun wa-lākin hal laki ṣabrun ʿalā firāqi wālidiki wa-ahliki
sentences.l: And he said: By God, none will reach you so long as there is in my chest a spirit; but have you patience for the parting-from your father and your family?
sentences.i: He said, "By God, no one shall touch you so long as there is breath in my body. But can you bear to part from your father and your people?"
sentences.n: وَاللَّهِ is the oath "by God" (the wa- of swearing). رُوح here is the breath of life. هَلْ لَكِ صَبْرٌ عَلَى "have you patience for" is the ordinary way to ask whether someone can bear something.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ نَعَمْ فَحَلَّفَهَا شَرْكَانُ وَتَعَاهَدَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: qālat naʿam fa-ḥallafahā Sharkānu wa-taʿāhadā ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: She said: Yes. And Sharkān made-her-swear, and the two pledged-to-each-other upon that.
sentences.i: "Yes," she said. Sharkān made her swear to it, and the two bound themselves by a covenant.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتِ الْأَنَ طَابَ قَلْبِي وَلَكِنْ بَقِيَ عَلَيْكَ شَرْطٌ آخَرُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālati al-āna ṭāba qalbī wa-lākin baqiya ʿalayka sharṭun ākharu
sentences.l: And she said: Now my heart is good, but there remains upon you another condition.
sentences.i: She said, "Now my heart is at ease, but one more condition remains for you."
sentences.n: الْأَنَ is printed with a plain hamza-alif here, where a few lines above the print has الْآنَ; it is the same word, "now", and we point what is printed. طَابَ قَلْبِي, "my heart is good", means "my heart is at ease".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَمَا هُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-mā huwa
sentences.l: And he said: And what is it?
sentences.i: He said, "What is it?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ إِنَّكَ تَرْجِعُ بِعَسْكَرِكَ إِلَى بِلَادِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu innaka tarjiʿu bi-ʿaskarika ilā bilādika
sentences.l: And she said to him: Indeed you return with your army to your lands.
sentences.i: She said to him, "You are to lead your army back to your own country."
sentences.n: إِنَّكَ تَرْجِعُ, "you will return", is a plain statement standing for a request or condition: "the condition is that you return".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا يَاسَيِّدَتِي إِنَّ أَبِي عُمَرَ بْنَ النُّعْمَانِ أَرْسَلَنِي إِلَى قِتَالِ وَالِدِكِ بِسَبَبِ الْمَالِ الَّذِي أَخَذَهُ وَمِنْ جُمْلَتِهِ ثَلَٰثُ خَرَ زَاتِ الْكِبَارِ الْكَثِيرَةِ الْبَرَكَاتِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā yāsayyidatī inna abī ʿUmara ibna al-Nuʿmāni arsalanī ilā qitāli wālidiki bi-sababi al-māli alladhī akhadhahu wa-min jumlatihi thalāthu khara zāti al-kibāri al-kathīrati al-barakāti
sentences.l: And he said to her: O my lady, my father ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān sent me to the fighting of your father because of the property which he took, and among the whole of it three jewels, the great ones, the many-of blessings.
sentences.i: He said to her, "My lady, my father ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān sent me to make war on your father over the wealth he took, and among it three great jewels of abundant blessing."
sentences.n: يَاسَيِّدَتِي is printed as one word (yā + sayyidatī). ثلث is printed without its alif: we read it as ثَلَٰثُ "three" (the dagger alif marks the missing long vowel), though it could also be ثُلُثُ "a third of". The printed خر زات is split across a space; it is خَرَزَات "jewels, beads", and we keep the split. الْكَثِيرَةِ الْبَرَكَاتِ, "the many-of blessings", describes jewels of great virtue.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ طِبْ نَفْسًا وَقَرَّعَيْنًا فَهَا أَنَا أُحَدِّثُكَ بِحَدِيثِهَا وَسَبَبِ مُعَادَاتِنَا لِمَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu ṭib nafsan wa-qarra ʿaynan fa-hā anā uḥaddithuka bi-ḥadīthihā wa-sababi muʿādātinā li-maliki al-Qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: And she said to him: Be good in soul and cool in eye; for here I [am] telling you its tale and the cause of our enmity to the king of Constantinople.
sentences.i: She said to him, "Set your mind at ease and be of good cheer. I will tell you the tale of the jewels and the reason for our enmity with the king of Constantinople."
sentences.n: طِبْ نَفْسًا وَقَرَّ عَيْنًا, "be good of soul and cool of eye", is a wish for calm and contentment. The print joins the second verb to its object as وقرعينا; we keep the single word. نَفْسًا and عَيْنًا are accusatives of respect. حَدِيثِهَا, "its tale", is the tale of the jewels.

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ لَنَا عِيدًا يُقَالُ لَهُ عِيدُ الدَّيْرِ فِي كُلِّ سَنَةٍ تَجْتَمِعُ فِيهِ الْمُلُوكُ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الْأَقْطَارِ وَبَنَاتُ الْأَكَابِرِ وَالتُّجَّارُ وَنِسَاؤُهُمْ وَيَقْعُدُونَ فِيهِ سَبْعَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَأَنَا مِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika anna lanā ʿīdan yuqālu lahu ʿīdu al-dayri fī kulli sanatin tajtamiʿu fīhi al-mulūku min jamīʿi al-aqṭāri wa-banātu al-akābiri wa-al-tujjāru wa-nisāʾuhum wa-yaqʿudūna fīhi sabʿata ayyāmin wa-anā min jumlatihim
sentences.l: And that [is] that we have a festival, it is said to it the Festival-of the Monastery; in every year there gather in it the kings from all the regions, and the daughters-of the great-ones, and the merchants and their women, and they stay in it seven days, and I [am] among the total of them.
sentences.i: It is like this: we have a festival called the Festival of the Monastery. Every year the kings gather at it from every land, together with the daughters of the nobles, the merchants and their wives, and they stay there seven days, and I am one of them.
sentences.n: وَذَلِكَ أَنَّ ... "and that is that ..." opens an explanation. عِيدُ الدَّيْرِ is the feast held at a monastery. يُقَالُ لَهُ, "it is said to it", is the usual way to give a name.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَقَعَتْ بَيْنَنَا الْمُعَادَاةُ مَنَعَنِي أَبِي مِنْ حُضُورِ ذَلِكَ الْعِيدِ مُدَّةَ سَبْعِ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waqaʿat baynanā al-muʿādātu manaʿanī abī min ḥuḍūri dhālika al-ʿīdi muddata sabʿi sinīna
sentences.l: And when there fell between us the enmity, my father prevented me from attendance of that festival, a period of seven years.
sentences.i: When enmity arose between us, my father kept me away from that festival for seven years.
sentences.n: The speaker is still Abrīza: because of the enmity between her father and the king of Constantinople, her father forbade her the yearly festival at the monastery. سِنِينَ is the sound masculine plural of سَنَة "year", used here after سَبْعِ in the genitive.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ فِي سَنَةٍ مِنَ السِّنِينَ أَنَّ بَنَاتِ الْأَكَابِرِ مِنْ سَائِرِ الْجِهَاتِ قَدْ جَاءَتْ مِنْ أَمَاكِنِهَا إِلَى الدَّيْرِ فِي ذَلِكَ الْعِيدِ عَلَى الْعَادَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa fī sanatin mina al-sinīna anna banāti al-akābiri min sāʾiri al-jihāti qad jāʾat min amākinihā ilā al-dayri fī dhālika al-ʿīdi ʿalā al-ʿādati
sentences.l: And it happened in a year of the years that the daughters of the great-ones, from all of the quarters, had come from their places to the monastery, in that festival, according to the custom.
sentences.i: Then in one of those years it happened that the daughters of the great, from every quarter, came from their homes to the monastery for that festival, as was the custom.
sentences.n: فَاتَّفَقَ فِي سَنَةٍ مِنَ السِّنِينَ, literally "it happened in a year of the years", is a stock way of saying "one year it happened that". جَاءَتْ is feminine singular, as Arabic regularly makes the verb agree with a non-human or collective plural.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ جُمْلَةِ مَنْ جَاءَ إِلَيْهِ بِنْتُ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ وَهِيَ بِنْتٌ جَمِيلَةٌ يُقَالُ لَهَا صَفِيَّةُ
sentences.tr: wa-min jumlati man jāʾa ilayhi bintu maliki al-Qusṭanṭīniyyati wa-hiya bintun jamīlatun yuqālu lahā Ṣafiyyatu
sentences.l: And from the totality of whoever came to it, the daughter of the king of Constantinople, and she a daughter, beautiful, it is said to her Ṣafiyya.
sentences.i: Among those who came was the daughter of the king of Constantinople, a beautiful girl called Ṣafiyya.
sentences.n: مِنْ جُمْلَةِ مَنْ جَاءَ, literally "from the sum of those who came", means "among those who came". The verb is masculine (جَاءَ) because مَنْ takes masculine agreement even for a group of women.

sentences.t: فَأَقَامُوا فِي الدَّيْرِ سِتَّةَ أَيَّامٍ وَفِى الْيَوْمِ السَّابِعِ انْصَرَفَتِ النَّاسُ
sentences.tr: fa-aqāmū fī al-dayri sittata ayyāmin wa-fī al-yawmi al-sābiʿi inṣarafati al-nāsu
sentences.l: And they stayed in the monastery six days, and on the day, the seventh, the people went away.
sentences.i: They stayed at the monastery for six days, and on the seventh day the people departed.
sentences.n: انْصَرَفَتِ النَّاسُ gives "the people" a feminine verb. That is a Middle Arabic habit, treating a collective as feminine singular, and we vocalise it as printed. The printed أ in أَيَّام is the edition's own; فِي is printed with a dotless final letter (فى), a common spelling of the preposition in this text.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ صَفِيَّةُ أَنَا مَا أَرْجِعُ إِلَى الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ إِلَّا فِى الْبَحْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat Ṣafiyyatu anā mā arjiʿu ilā al-Qusṭanṭīniyyati illā fī al-baḥri
sentences.l: And said Ṣafiyya: I, I will not return to Constantinople except in the sea.
sentences.i: Ṣafiyya said, "I will go back to Constantinople only by sea."
sentences.n: مَا أَرْجِعُ ... إِلَّا فِي الْبَحْرِ is the "not ... except" pattern. فِي الْبَحْرِ, "in the sea", means travelling by sea.

sentences.t: فَجَهَّزُوا لَهَا مَرْكَبًا وَنَزَلَتْ هِيَ وَخَوَاصُّهَا
sentences.tr: fa-jahhazū lahā markaban wa-nazalat hiya wa-khawāṣṣuhā
sentences.l: So they equipped for her a ship, and she embarked, she and her intimates.
sentences.i: So they fitted out a ship for her, and she went aboard with her attendants.
sentences.n: خَوَاصّ (plural of خَاصَّة) means her special ones, her close retinue.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَلُّوا الْقُلُوعَ وَسَارُوا فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ سَائِرُونَ وَإِذَا بِرِيحٍ قَدْ خَرَجَ عَلَيْهِمْ فَأَخْرَجَ الْمَرْكَبَ عَنْ طَرِيقِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥallū al-qulūʿa wa-sārū fa-baynamā hum sāʾirūna wa-idhā bi-rīḥin qad kharaja ʿalayhim fa-akhraja al-markaba ʿan ṭarīqihi
sentences.l: And when they loosed the sails and journeyed, then while they were journeying, and behold, with a wind had come out upon them, and it put-out the ship from its road.
sentences.i: When they had unfurled the sails and set out, and while they were sailing along, a wind burst upon them and drove the ship off its course.
sentences.n: The sentence starts with فَلَمَّا but never supplies its main clause, because the second فَبَيْنَمَا takes over: a loose construction we keep as printed. وَإِذَا بِرِيحٍ is the "and behold" idiom, where بِـ after إِذَا only marks what appears; وَإِذَا follows بَيْنَمَا هُمْ سَائِرُونَ as its "suddenly".

sentences.t: وَكَانَ هُنَاكَ بِالْقَضَاءِ وَالْقَدَرِ مَرْكَبُ نَصَارَى مِنْ جَزِيرَةِ الْكَافُورِ وَفِيهَا خَمْسُمِأَنَةِ أِفْرَنْجِيٍّ بِالسِّلَاحِ وَكَانَ لَهُمْ مُدَّةٌ فِى الْبَحْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna hunāka bi-al-qaḍāʾi wa-al-qadari markabu naṣārā min jazīrati al-kāfūri wa-fīhā khamsumiʾanati ifranjiyyin bi-al-silāḥi wa-kāna lahum muddatun fī al-baḥri
sentences.l: And there was there, by the decree and the destiny, a ship of Christians from the Isle of Camphor, and in it five-hundred Franks with the weapons, and there was to them a period in the sea.
sentences.i: By decree and destiny, there was also a ship of Christians from the Isle of Camphor, carrying five hundred Franks under arms, who had already been a long time at sea.
sentences.n: بِالْقَضَاءِ وَالْقَدَرِ, "by decree and destiny", is a pious way of saying "as fate would have it". خَمْسُمِأَنَةِ is the printed spelling of خَمْسُمِائَة "five hundred"; the extra ن looks like a slip or an odd variant, and we point it as printed. الْكَافُور is camphor; "the Isle of Camphor" is a name from the Nights' fabulous geography. إِفْرَنْجِيّ, "Frank", is the Arabic word for a western European. بِالسِّلَاحِ, "with the weapons", means fully armed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا لَاحَ لَهُمْ قَلْعُ الْمَرْكَبِ الَّتِي فِيهَا صَفِيَّةُ وَمَنْ مَعَهَا مِنَ الْبَنَاتِ انْقَضُّوا عَلَيْهَا مُسْرِعِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā lāḥa lahum qalʿu al-markabi allatī fīhā Ṣafiyyatu wa-man maʿahā mina al-banāti inqaḍḍū ʿalayhā musriʿīna
sentences.l: And when appeared to them the sail of the ship which in it Ṣafiyya and whoever with her of the girls, they swooped upon it, hastening.
sentences.i: When they sighted the sail of the ship that carried Ṣafiyya and the girls with her, they swooped down on it at speed.
sentences.n: الْمَرْكَب is treated here as feminine (الَّتِي, عَلَيْهَا), though the word is normally masculine. We point the relative as printed.

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَ دُونَ سَاعَةٍ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى تِلْكَ الْمَرْكَبِ وَوَضَعُوا فِيهَا الْكَلَالِيبَ وَجَرُّوهَا
sentences.tr: fa-mā kāna dūna sāʿatin ḥattā waṣalū ilā tilka al-markabi wa-waḍaʿū fīhā al-kalālība wa-jarrūhā
sentences.l: And it was not less than an hour until they reached that ship, and put into it the grappling-hooks, and dragged it.
sentences.i: Within an hour they had reached that ship, fixed their grappling hooks in it and hauled it along.
sentences.n: فَمَا كَانَ دُونَ سَاعَةٍ, literally "it was not less than an hour", means "it took no more than an hour". الْكَلَالِيب (plural of كُلَّاب) are grappling hooks.

sentences.t: وَحَلُّوا قُلُوعَهُمْ وَقَصَدُ وْاجَزِيرَتَهُمْ فَمَا بَعُدُوا غَيْرَ قَلِيلٍ حَتَّى انْعَكَسَ الرِّيحُ عَلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-ḥallū qulūʿahum wa-qaṣadū jazīratahum fa-mā baʿudū ghayra qalīlin ḥattā inʿakasa al-rīḥu ʿalayhim
sentences.l: And they loosed their sails and made-for their island, and they did not go-far other than a little until the wind turned about upon them.
sentences.i: They spread their sails and made for their island, but they had gone only a little way when the wind turned against them.
sentences.n: The edition prints the end of قَصَدُوا wrongly joined to the next word: قصد واجزيرتهم, that is, قَصَدُوا جَزِيرَتَهُمْ with the plural wāw-alif attached to the following noun. We keep the printed spacing and point the wāw as the verb's ending (سكون), with the alif silent. غَيْرَ قَلِيلٍ means "only a little". الرِّيح is masculine here, as in the next unit; the classical gender is feminine.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا انْعَكَسَ الرِّيحُ عَلَيْهِمْ جَذَبَهُمْ إِلَى شِعْبٍ وَ خَرَقَ الرِّيحُ قُلُوعَهُمْ وَجَرَّهُمْ إِلَيْنَا غَصْبًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā inʿakasa al-rīḥu ʿalayhim jadhabahum ilā shiʿbin wa- kharaqa al-rīḥu qulūʿahum wa-jarrahum ilaynā ghaṣban
sentences.l: And when the wind turned about upon them, it drew them to a mountain-pass, and tore the wind their sails, and dragged them to us by force.
sentences.i: When the wind turned against them it pulled them toward a rocky channel, shredded their sails, and dragged them to us by force.
sentences.n: The edition splits the word وَخَرَقَ across a line break (و / خرق), and we keep it split. شِعْب can mean a mountain pass or a cleft; here it probably means a rocky channel by the shore. غَصْبًا is "by force, perforce".

sentences.t: فَخَرَجْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ فَرَأَيْنَاهُمْ غَنِيمَةً قَدِ انْسَاقَتْ إِلَيْنَا
sentences.tr: fa-kharajnā ilayhim fa-raʾaynāhum ghanīmatan qadi insāqat ilaynā
sentences.l: And we went out to them, and we saw them a booty which had been driven to us.
sentences.i: We went out to them and saw them as spoil that had been driven right to us.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ وَقَتَلْنَاهُمْ فَوَجَدْنَا تِلْكَ الْأَمْوَالَ وَالتُّحَفَ وَأَرْبَعِينَ جَارِيَةً وَمِنْ جُمْلَتِهِمْ صَفِيَّةُ بِنْتُ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhnāhum wa-qatalnāhum fa-wajadnā tilka al-amwāla wa-al-tuḥafa wa-arbaʿīna jāriyatan wa-min jumlatihim Ṣafiyyatu bintu al-maliki
sentences.l: And we seized them and killed them, and we found those goods, and the rarities, and forty girls, and among them Ṣafiyya, daughter of the king.
sentences.i: We seized them and killed them, and found the goods and treasures, and forty slave girls, among them Ṣafiyya, the king's daughter.
sentences.n: الْجَارِيَة means a young woman, especially a slave girl, and the edition uses it constantly for the women taken in raids. التُّحَف (plural of تُحْفَة) are rare and precious things.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ وَقَدَّمْنَا الْجَوَارِيَ إِلَى أَبِي
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhnāhum wa-qaddamnā al-jawāriya ilā abī
sentences.l: And we took them, and presented the girls to my father.
sentences.i: We took them, and presented the girls to my father,
sentences.n: Here the edition repeats فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ, "and we took them", with the girls now the object; we translate it as the plain next step in the narrative.

sentences.t: وَنَحْنُ مَا نَعْرِفُ أَنَّ فِيهِنَّ ابْنَةَ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-naḥnu mā naʿrifu anna fīhinna ibnata al-maliki Afrīdūna maliki al-Qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: And we, we did not know that among them [was] the daughter of the king Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople.
sentences.i: We had no idea that among them was the daughter of King Afrīdūn, ruler of Constantinople.
sentences.n: مَا نَعْرِفُ is a present tense with past sense, "we did not know": the same Middle Arabic use of مَا + present as in the rest of the passage. وَنَحْنُ ... marks a circumstantial clause, "while we did not know".

sentences.t: فَاخْتَارَ أَبِي مِنْهُنَّ عَشْرَ جَوَارٍ وَفِيهِنَّ ابْنَةُ الْمَلِكِ وَفَرَّقَ الْبَاقِيَ عَلَى حَاشِيَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ikhtāra abī minhunna ʿashra jawārin wa-fīhinna ibnatu al-maliki wa-farraqa al-bāqiya ʿalā ḥāshiyatihi
sentences.l: And my father chose from among them ten girls, and among them the daughter of the king, and distributed the rest among his retinue.
sentences.i: My father chose ten of them, among whom was the king's daughter, and shared out the rest among his household.
sentences.n: عَشْرَ جَوَارٍ is printed with the plural جَوَارٍ without a tanwīn-bearing ي, as the classical diptote جَوَارٍ requires; so "ten girls" is read with the noun in the genitive.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ عَزَلَ خَمْسَةَ جَوَارٍ فِيهِنَّ ابْنَةُ الْمَلِكِ وَأَرْسَلَهُنَّ هَدِيَّةً إِلَى وَالِدِكَ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ مَعَ شَيٍّ مِنَ الْجُوخِ وَمِنْ ثِيَابِ الصُّوفِ وَمِنَ الْقُمَاشِ الْحَرِيرِ الرُّومِيِّ
sentences.tr: thumma ʿazala khamsata jawārin fīhinna ibnatu al-maliki wa-arsalahunna hadiyyatan ilā wālidika ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni maʿa shayyin mina al-jūkhi wa-min thiyābi al-ṣūfi wa-mina al-qumāshi al-ḥarīri al-rūmiyyi
sentences.l: Then he set-apart five girls, among them the daughter of the king, and sent them as a gift to your father ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, with something of broadcloth and of garments of wool and of the cloth, the silk, the Rūmī.
sentences.i: Then he set aside five girls, the king's daughter among them, and sent them as a gift to your father, ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, together with some broadcloth, woollen garments, and Greek silk fabric.
sentences.n: The speaker is now addressing a listener whose father is ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. شَيّ is the printed spelling of شَيْء, the hamza dropped; we point it as printed. الْجُوخ is broadcloth. الْقُمَاش is fabric, and الْحَرِير is silk. الرُّومِيّ, "Rūmī", means Byzantine, that is, from the Greek-speaking Christian empire.

sentences.t: وَقَبِلَهُ أَبُوكَ فَاخْتَارَ مِنَ الْخَمْسِ جَوَارٍ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتَ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-qabilahu abūka fa-ikhtāra mina al-khamsi jawārin Ṣafiyyata binta al-maliki Afrīdūna
sentences.l: And your father accepted it, and chose from the five girls Ṣafiyya, daughter of the king Afrīdūn.
sentences.i: Your father accepted it, and out of the five girls he chose Ṣafiyya, daughter of King Afrīdūn.
sentences.n: مِنَ الْخَمْسِ جَوَارٍ pairs the definite article with an indefinite counted noun, "from the five girls"; this is the Middle Arabic way and we do not correct it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ أَوَّلُ هَذَا الْعَامِ كَتَبَ أَبُوهَا كِتَابًا إِلَى وَالِدِي بِكَلَامٍ لَايَنْبَغِي ذِكْرُهُ وَصَارَ يُهَدِّدُهُ وَيُوَبِّخُهُ وَيَقُولُ لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna awwalu hādhā al-ʿāmi kataba abūhā kitāban ilā wālidī bi-kalāmin lā yanbaghī dhikruhu wa-ṣāra yuhaddiduhu wa-yuwabbikhuhu wa-yaqūlu lahu
sentences.l: And when it was the beginning of this year, her father wrote a letter to my father with speech which is not fitting its mentioning, and he began threatening him and rebuking him and saying to him:
sentences.i: At the beginning of this year her father wrote a letter to my father in words not fit to repeat, threatening and reproaching him, and saying to him:
sentences.n: كَانَ here means "came": "when the beginning of this year came". لَايَنْبَغِي is printed as one word, لَا يَنْبَغِي, "it is not fitting". صَارَ يُهَدِّدُهُ, "he became threatening him", means "he went on to threaten him".

sentences.t: أَنْتُمْ رَبِحْتُمْ مِنَّا مَرْكَبًا مِنْ مُنْذُ سَنَتَيْنِ وَكَانَتْ فِي يَدِ لُصُوصٍ مِنْ جَمَاعَةِ أَفْرَنْجٍ حَرَامِيَّةٍ وَكَانَتْ فِيهَا بِنْتِي صَفِيَّةُ وَمَعَهَا مِنَ الْجَوَارِي نَحْوَ سِتِّينَ جَارِيَةً
sentences.tr: antum rabiḥtum minnā markaban min mundhu sanatayni wa-kānat fī yadi luṣūṣin min jamāʿati afranjin ḥarāmiyyatin wa-kānat fīhā bintī Ṣafiyyatu wa-maʿahā mina al-jawārī naḥwa sittīna jāriyatan
sentences.l: You, you gained from us a ship since two years, and it was in the hand of thieves from a band of Franks, brigands, and in it was my daughter Ṣafiyya, and with her of the girls about sixty girls.
sentences.i: "You have profited from us by a ship, two years ago, which was in the hands of thieves from a band of Frankish brigands; and in it was my daughter Ṣafiyya, and with her some sixty slave girls.
sentences.n: مِنْ مُنْذُ سَنَتَيْنِ is a doubled preposition, "from since two years", meaning "for two years now". رَبِحْتُمْ مِنَّا is "you gained at our expense". حَرَامِيَّة ("brigands") is a colloquial plural of حَرَامِيّ, a common word for thieves in the Nights. This is a letter, so the speech is Afrīdūn's own, quoted by the speaker.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ تُعْلِمُونِي وَلَمْ تُرْسِلُوا إِلَيَّ أَحَدًا يُخْبِرُنِي بِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-lam tuʿlimūnī wa-lam tursilū ilayya aḥadan yukhbirunī bi-dhālika
sentences.l: And you did not inform me, and you did not send to me anyone who might tell me of that.
sentences.i: You never told me, and never sent anyone to let me know of it.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا لَمْ أَقْدِرْ أُظْهِرُ الْخَبَرَ خَوْفًا أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي حَقِّي عَارٌ عِنْدَ الْمُلُوكِ مِنْ أَجْلِ هَتْكِ ابْنَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-anā lam aqdir uẓhiru al-khabara khawfan an yakūna fī ḥaqqī ʿārun ʿinda al-mulūki min ajli hatki ibnatī
sentences.l: And I, I was not able I make-known the news, out of fear that there be in my right a shame with the kings because of the violation of my daughter.
sentences.i: And I could not make the news public, for fear that it would bring shame on me among the kings because of my daughter's dishonour.
sentences.n: لَمْ أَقْدِرْ أُظْهِرُ has two verbs placed side by side with no linking أَنْ, "I could not (I) reveal", a Middle Arabic habit we keep. فِي حَقِّي, literally "in my right", means "in my regard", "as regards me". هَتْك is the tearing of a veil, so the violation of a woman's honour; it recurs in the letter.

sentences.t: فَكَتَمْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَى هَذَا الْعَامِ فَكَاتَبْتُ بَعْضَ الْحَرَامِيَّةِ مِنَ الْأَفْرَنْجِ وَسَأَلْتُهُمْ خَبَرَ ابْنَتِي عِنْدَ مَنْ فِى الْجَزَائِرِ مِنَ الْمُلُوكِ فَقَالُوا
sentences.tr: fa-katamtu amrī ilā hādhā al-ʿāmi fa-kātabtu baʿḍa al-ḥarāmiyyati mina al-afranji wa-saʾaltuhum khabara ibnatī ʿinda man fī al-jazāʾiri mina al-mulūki fa-qālū
sentences.l: So I concealed my affair until this year, and I corresponded with some of the brigands from the Franks, and I asked them the news of my daughter, with whom among those in the islands of the kings, and they said:
sentences.i: So I kept my trouble secret until this year, and then I wrote to some of the Frankish brigands and asked them for news of my daughter, and which of the kings in the islands had her. They said:
sentences.n: عِنْدَ مَنْ فِي الْجَزَائِرِ مِنَ الْمُلُوكِ is "with which of the kings who are in the islands". The letter is still Afrīdūn's own account of what he did.

sentences.t: وَاللَّهِ مَا خَرَجْنَا بِهَا مِنْ بِلَادِكَ لَكِنْ سَمِعْنَا أَنَّهَا أَخَذَهَا مِنْ يَدِ بَعْضِ الْحَرَامِيَّةِ مَلِكٌ حُرْ دُوبَ وَحَكَوْا لَهُ الْحِكَايَةَ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi mā kharajnā bi-hā min bilādika lākin samiʿnā annahā akhadhahā min yadi baʿḍi al-ḥarāmiyyati malikun Ḥur Dūba wa-ḥakaw lahu al-ḥikāyata
sentences.l: By God, we did not go out with her from your lands, but we heard that there took her from the hand of some of the brigands a king, Ḥardūb (printed Ḥur Dūb); and they told him the tale.
sentences.i: 'By God, we never took her out of your country, but we heard that a king, Ḥardūb, took her from the hands of some brigands, and they told him the story.'
sentences.n: The name مَلِكٌ حُرْ دُوبَ is printed as two words, and this is evidently Ḥardūb, Abrīza's father (sentence 28), whose name the print splits and spells with ḥu-; we point the two parts as printed. أَخَذَهَا ... مَلِكٌ puts the verb before its subject, so the king is the one who took her. The speech ends with وَحَكَوْا لَهُ الْحِكَايَةَ, "and they told him the story".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ فِى الْمَكْتُوبِ الَّذِي كَتَبَهُ لِوَالِدِي إِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ مُرَادُكُمْ مُعَادَ اتِي وَقَصْدُكُمْ فَضِيحَتِي وَهَتْكَ ابْنَتِي فَسَاعَةَ وُصُولِ كِتَابِي إِلَيْكُمْ تُرْسِلُوا إِلَيَّ ابْنَتِي مِنْ عِنْدِكُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla fī al-maktūbi alladhī katabahu li-wālidī in lam yakun murādukum muʿādātī wa-qaṣdukum faḍīḥatī wa-hatka ibnatī fa-sāʿata wuṣūli kitābī ilaykum tursilū ilayya ibnatī min ʿindikum
sentences.l: Then he said in the letter which he wrote to my father: If your intent is not my enmity and your aim my disgrace and the violation of my daughter, then at the hour of the arrival of my letter to you, send to me my daughter from you.
sentences.i: Then he said in the letter he wrote to my father: If you do not mean to be my enemies, to shame me and violate my daughter, then the moment my letter reaches you, send my daughter back to me from your side.
sentences.n: معاد اتي is printed as two words; it is مُعَادَاتِي, "my enmity", the abstract noun from عَادَى "to be hostile", cut apart by a space. تُرْسِلُوا is printed without the final nūn of تُرْسِلُونَ; here it stands as a command in the main clause after the if-clause, so the dropped nūn may mark an imperative-like sense, "you are to send". We point it as printed.

sentences.t: وَإِنْ أَهْمَلْتُمْ كِتَابِي وَعَصَيْتُمْ أَمْرِي فَلَا بُدَّأَنْ أُكَافِئَكُمْ عَلَى قَبِيحِ أَفْعَالِكُمْ وَسُوءِ أَعْمَالِكُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-in ahmaltum kitābī wa-ʿaṣaytum amrī fa-lā budda an ukāfiʾakum ʿalā qabīḥi afʿālikum wa-sūʾi aʿmālikum
sentences.l: And if you neglect my letter and disobey my command, then there is no escape that I repay you for the ugliness of your deeds and the evil of your works.
sentences.i: But if you ignore my letter and defy my order, then I will surely repay you for your vile deeds and your wicked works."
sentences.n: فَلَا بُدَّأَنْ is printed as one word for فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ, "there is no escaping that", that is, "I shall certainly". أُكَافِئَكُمْ is "I repay you", and with عَلَى it means repaying evil with evil. قَبِيحِ أَفْعَالِكُمْ وَسُوءِ أَعْمَالِكُمْ is a rhyming pair, أَفْعَال / أَعْمَال.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَتْ هَذِهِ الْمُكَاتَبَةُ إِلَى أَبِي وَقَرَأَهَا وَفَهِمَ مَا فِيهَا شَقَّ عَلَيْهِ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣalat hādhihi al-mukātabatu ilā abī wa-qaraʾahā wa-fahima mā fīhā shaqqa ʿalayhi dhālika
sentences.l: And when this correspondence reached my father and he read it and understood what was in it, that was hard upon him.
sentences.i: When this letter reached my father and he had read it and understood what it held, it weighed heavily on him,
sentences.n: شَقَّ عَلَيْهِ is the idiom "it was hard on him", "it distressed him".

sentences.t: وَنَدِمَ حَيْثُ لَمْ يَعْرِفْ أَنَّ صَفِيَّةَ بِنْتَ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ فِي تِلْكَ الْجَوَارِي لِيَرُدَّهَا إِلَى وَالِدِهَا فَتَحَيَّرَ فِي أَمْرِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-nadima ḥaythu lam yaʿrif anna Ṣafiyyata binta al-maliki Afrīdūna fī tilka al-jawārī li-yaruddahā ilā wālidihā fa-taḥayyara fī amrihi
sentences.l: And he regretted that he had not known that Ṣafiyya, daughter of the king Afrīdūn, was among those girls, so that he might return her to her father, and he was perplexed in his affair.
sentences.i: and he regretted not having known that Ṣafiyya, daughter of King Afrīdūn, was among those girls, for he would have sent her back to her father; and he was at a loss what to do.
sentences.n: حَيْثُ here means "since, because", not "where". لِيَرُدَّهَا, "so that he might return her", carries the sense "otherwise he would have returned her".

sentences.t: وَمَابَقِيَ يُمْكِنُهُ بَعْدَ هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةِ الْكَبِيرَةِ أَنْ يُرْسِلَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ يَطْلُبُهَا مِنْهُ وَلَاسِيَّمَا أَنَّنَا سَمِعْنَا مِنْ مُدَّةٍ يَسِيرَةٍ أَنَّهُ رُزِقَ مِنْ جَارِيَتِهِ الَّتِي يُقَالُ لَهَا صَفِيَّةُ بِنْتُ الْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ أَوْلَادًا
sentences.tr: wa-mābaqiya yumkinuhu baʿda hādhihi al-muddati al-kabīrati an yursila ilā al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni yaṭlubuhā minhu wa-lāsiyyamā annanā samiʿnā min muddatin yasīratin annahu ruziqa min jāriyatihi allatī yuqālu lahā Ṣafiyyatu bintu al-maliki Afrīdūna awlādan
sentences.l: And not-remained possible-for-him after this great period that he send to King ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān, asking-for-her from him, and especially that we heard, from a short period, that he was provided, from his slave-girl who is said to-her Ṣafiyya, daughter-of King Afrīdūn, with children.
sentences.i: And after so long a time he could no longer send to King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān to ask for her back, especially since we heard, only a short while ago, that he has been granted children by his slave girl, the one called Ṣafiyya, daughter of King Afrīdūn.
sentences.n: This sentence continues from the previous line, where Abrīza is telling Sharkān the story. وَمَابَقِيَ and وَلَاسِيَّمَا are each printed as one word (mā baqiya, "no longer"; lā siyyamā, "especially"). رُزِقَ مِنْ means "was granted (children) by"; the children are the object أَوْلَادًا at the end.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَحَقَّقْنَا ذَلِكَ عَلِمْنَا أَنَّ هَذِهِ الْوَرَقَةَ هِيَ الْمُصِيبَةُ الْعُظْمَى
sentences.tr: fa-lammā taḥaqqaqnā dhālika ʿalimnā anna hādhihi al-waraqata hiya al-muṣībatu al-ʿuẓmā
sentences.l: And when we made-sure of that, we knew that this paper, it is the calamity, the greatest.
sentences.i: When we were sure of it, we knew that this letter was the greatest of calamities.
sentences.n: الْوَرَقَةَ, literally "the sheet", means the letter that Afrīdūn's messengers have carried to ʿUmar. الْمُصِيبَةُ الْعُظْمَى is the superlative construction "the greatest calamity".

sentences.t: فَمَا كَانَ لِأَبِي حِيلَةٌ غَيْرَأَنَّهُ كَتَبَ جَوَابًا لِلْمَلِكِ أَفْرِيدُونَ وَيَعْتَذِرُ إِلَيْهِ وَيَحْلِفُ لَهُ بِالْأَقْسَامِ أَنَّهُ مَا عَلِمَ أَنَّ ابْنَتَهُ كَانَتْ مِنْ جُمْلَةِ الْجَوَارِي الَّتِي كَانَتْ فِي تِلْكَ الْمَرْكَبِ ثُمَّ أَظْهَرَهُ عَلَى أَنَّهُ أَرْسَلَهَا إِلَى الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَأَنَّهُ رُزِقَ مِنْهَا الْأَوْلَادَ
sentences.tr: fa-mā kāna li-abī ḥīlatun ghayra annahu kataba jawāban li-al-maliki Afrīdūna wa-yaʿtadhiru ilayhi wa-yaḥlifu lahu bi-al-aqsāmi annahu mā ʿalima anna ibnatahu kānat min jumlati al-jawārī allatī kānat fī tilka al-markabi thumma aẓharahu ʿalā annahu arsalahā ilā al-maliki ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni wa-annahu ruziqa minhā al-awlāda
sentences.l: And not was for my father any contrivance except-that he wrote an answer to King Afrīdūn, and he excuses himself to him, and swears to him by the oaths that he did not know that his daughter was among the sum of the slave-girls who were in that ship; then he informed him that he had sent her to King ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān, and that he was provided from her with the children.
sentences.i: My father had no recourse but to write an answer to King Afrīdūn, making his excuses and swearing to him by solemn oaths that he had not known that his daughter was among the slave girls aboard that ship. Then he told him that he had sent her on to King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and that she had borne him children.
sentences.n: Here "my father" is Abrīza's own father. غَيْرَأَنَّهُ is printed as one word (ghayra annahu, "except that"). The verbs وَيَعْتَذِرُ and وَيَحْلِفُ are present tense after a past كَتَبَ, which is Middle Arabic for "and (he) excuses himself and swears"; read them as part of the same narrative. تِلْكَ الْمَرْكَبِ treats مَرْكَب ("ship") as feminine. أَظْهَرَهُ عَلَى is "informed him of".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَتْ رِسَالَةُ أَبِي إِلَى أَفْرِيدُونَ مَلِكِ الْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ قَامَ وَقَعَدُوا رَغَى وَأَزْبَدَ وَقَالَ كَيْفَ أَنَّهُ سَبَي ابْنَتِي وَصَارَتْ بِصِفَةِ الْجَوَارِي وَتَتَدَاوَلُهَا الْأَيْدِي وَتَصِلُ إِلَي الْمُلُوكِ وَيَطَؤُنَهَا بِلَا عَقْدٍ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣalat risālatu abī ilā Afrīdūna maliki al-Qusṭanṭīniyyati qāma wa-qaʿadū raghā wa-azbada wa-qāla kayfa annahu sabā ibnatī wa-ṣārat bi-ṣifati al-jawārī wa-tatadāwaluhā al-aydī wa-taṣilu ilā al-mulūki wa-yaṭaʾunahā bi-lā ʿaqdin
sentences.l: And when the letter of my father reached Afrīdūn, king-of Constantinople, he rose, and sat-they, raged, and foamed, and said: How is it that he has taken-captive my daughter, and she has become in the guise of the slave-girls, and the hands pass her around, and she reaches to the kings, and they tread her without a contract?
sentences.i: When my father's letter reached Afrīdūn, king of Constantinople, he leapt up and sat down again, roaring and foaming at the mouth, and said, "How can he have taken my daughter captive, so that she has become like any slave girl, passed from hand to hand, sent on to kings, who lie with her without any marriage contract?"
sentences.n: The printed وَقَعَدُوا رَغَى is a slip: the word is surely وَقَعَدَ وَرَغَى, "and sat, and roared", with a stray alif and the wāw detached, but we point the letters as printed (a plural "they sat") and translate it as the singular the sense needs. رَغَى (the camel's roar) and أَزْبَدَ ("foamed") are the stock pair for a man in a rage. سَبَي and إِلَي are printed with a dotted yāʾ where the classical spelling has ى; we point them as printed. يَطَؤُنَهَا is the printed spelling of what would classically be يَطَؤُونَهَا, "they tread her", a blunt verb for sexual intercourse, here as elsewhere translated as what it is. بِلَا عَقْدٍ means "without a (marriage) contract".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ وَالدِّينِ الصَّحِيحِ مَا بَقِيتُ أَقْعُدُ عَنْ هَذَا إِلَّا أَنْ آخُذَ الثَّأْرَ وَأَكْشِفَ الْعَارَ وَإِنِّي لَأَ فْعَلَنَّ فِعْلًا يَتَحَدَّثُونَ بِهِ الْمُحَدِّثُونَ مِنْ بَعْدِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-ḥaqqi al-masīḥi wa-al-dīni al-ṣaḥīḥi mā baqītu aqʿudu ʿan hādhā illā an ākhudha al-thaʾra wa-akshifa al-ʿāra wa-innī la-afʿalanna fiʿlan yataḥaddathūna bihi al-muḥaddithūna min baʿdī
sentences.l: And he said: By the right of the Messiah and the religion, the true: I will not remain sitting from this, except that I take the vengeance and uncover the shame; and indeed I, I will surely do a deed that they will talk about, the talkers, after me.
sentences.i: Then he said, "By the Messiah and the true faith, I will not sit idle over this until I have taken vengeance and wiped away the shame. I swear I will do a deed that the storytellers will be telling of after I am gone."
sentences.n: وَحَقِّ الْمَسِيحِ is an oath, "by the right of the Messiah". The edition prints لَأَ فْعَلَنَّ as two words, لا فعلن; read it as the single emphatic لَأَفْعَلَنَّ, "I will surely do". يَتَحَدَّثُونَ بِهِ الْمُحَدِّثُونَ repeats the subject ("they will talk of it, the talkers"), a common emphatic order in this text.

sentences.t: وَمَا زَالَ صَابِرًا إِلَى أَنْ دَبَّرَ الْحِيلَةَ وَنَصَبَ مَكَائِدَ عَظِيمَةً وَأَرْسَلَ رُسُلًا إِلَى وَالِدِكَ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَذَكَرَ لَهُ مَا سَمِعْتُ مِنَ الْأَقْوَالِ حَتَّى أَنَّ وَالِدَكَ جَهَّزَكَ بِالْعَسَاكِرِ الَّتِي مَعَكَ مِنْ أَجْلِهَا وَصَيَّرَكَ إِلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَقْبِضَ عَلَيْكَ وَمَنْ مَعَكَ مِنْ عَسْكَرِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zāla ṣābiran ilā an dabbara al-ḥīlata wa-naṣaba makāʾida ʿaẓīmatan wa-arsala rusulan ilā wālidika ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni wa-dhakara lahu mā samiʿtu mina al-aqwāli ḥattā anna wālidaka jahhazaka bi-al-ʿasākiri allatī maʿaka min ajlihā wa-ṣayyaraka ilayhi ḥattā yaqbiḍa ʿalayka wa-man maʿaka min ʿaskarika
sentences.l: And he did not cease patient until he devised the stratagem, and set great snares, and sent messengers to your father ʿUmar son-of al-Nuʿmān, and mentioned to him what I heard of the sayings, until your father equipped you with the armies that are with you, for her sake, and turned you to him, so that he seize you and whoever is with you of your army.
sentences.i: But he kept his patience until he had worked out his stratagem and laid great snares. He sent envoys to your father, ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and told him the stories I have heard, until your father fitted you out with the armies that are with you, on her account, and sent you to him, so that he could seize you and all who are with you.
sentences.n: سَمِعْتُ is unpointed in the print, so the speaker could be "I" (Abrīza) or "you" (سَمِعْتَ); we read "I" and the sense is the rumours Afrīdūn's envoys told ʿUmar. مِنْ أَجْلِهَا, "for her sake", is vague about whom or what it means; presumably Ṣafiyya, or the beads of the next sentence. صَيَّرَكَ إِلَيْهِ, "turned you to him", means that ʿUmar sent Sharkān off toward Afrīdūn.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا ثَلٰثُ خَرَزَاتٍ الَّتِي قَالَ لِوَالِدِكَ عَنْهَا فِي سَالَتِهِ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِذَلِكَ صِحَّةٌ وَإِنَّمَا كَانَتْ مَعَ صَفِيَّةَ ابْنَتِهِ وَأَخَذَهَا أَبِي مِنْهَا حِينَ اسْتَوْلَى عَلَيْهَا هِيَ وَالْجَوَارِي الَّتِي مَعَهَا وَوَهَبَهَا لِي وَهِيَ الْآنَ عِنْدِي
sentences.tr: wa-ammā thalāthu kharazātin allatī qāla li-wālidika ʿanhā fī sālatihi lam yakun li-dhālika ṣiḥḥatun wa-innamā kānat maʿa Ṣafiyyata ibnatihi wa-akhadhahā abī minhā ḥīna istawlā ʿalayhā hiya wa-al-jawārī allatī maʿahā wa-wahabahā lī wa-hiya al-āna ʿindī
sentences.l: And as for three beads, which he said to your father about them in his letter, there was not for that any truth; and only they were with Ṣafiyya his daughter, and my father took them from her when he gained-mastery over her, she and the slave-girls who were with her, and gave them to me, and they are now with me.
sentences.i: As for the three beads he mentioned to your father in his letter, there was no truth in that. They were in fact with his daughter Ṣafiyya, and my father took them from her when he seized her and the slave girls with her, and he gave them to me. I have them now.
sentences.n: ثَلٰثُ خَرَزَاتٍ is printed ثلث, a defective spelling of ثَلَاث, so it carries the dagger alif; the construction is indefinite although the relative الَّتِي follows ("the three beads which"). سَالَتِهِ is as printed: it is evidently رِسَالَتِهِ, "his letter", with the first letter dropped. Note that "he" in قَالَ لِوَالِدِكَ is Afrīdūn. The pronouns referring back to the beads ("them" in the translation) are feminine singular, as Arabic treats plural things.

sentences.t: فَاذْهَبْ أَنْتَ إِلَى عَسْكَرِكَ وَرُدَّهُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَسْتَغْرِقُوا وَيَتَوَغَّلُوا فِي بِلَادِ الْأَفْرَنْجِ وَالرُّومِ فَإِنَّكُمْ إِذَا تَوَغَّلْتُمْ فِي بِلَادِهِمْ يُضَيِّقُونَ عَلَيْكُمُ الطُّرُقَ فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا لَهُمْ خَلَاصًا مِنْ أَيْدِيهِمْ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْجَزَاءِ وَالْقِصَاصِ
sentences.tr: fa-idhhab anta ilā ʿaskarika wa-ruddahum qabla an yastaghriqū wa-yatawaghghalū fī bilādi al-Afranji wa-al-Rūmi fa-innakum idhā tawaghghaltum fī bilādihim yuḍayyiqūna ʿalaykumu al-ṭuruqa fa-lam tajidū lahum khalāṣan min aydīhim ilā yawmi al-jazāʾi wa-al-qiṣāṣi
sentences.l: So go, you, to your army, and turn them back before they go-deep and press-far into the lands of the Franks and the Rūm; for you, when you press far into their lands, they will narrow the roads upon you, and you will not find for them any deliverance from their hands until the day of requital and retribution.
sentences.i: So go back to your army, and turn them around before they venture deep into the lands of the Franks and the Rūm. If you press on into their country, they will close the roads around you, and you will find no escape from their hands until the Day of Requital and Reckoning.
sentences.n: الْأَفْرَنْجِ are the Franks, the Latin Christians of western Europe, and الرُّومِ the Byzantine Greeks; the text often runs the two together as "the Christians". يَوْمُ الْجَزَاءِ وَالْقِصَاصِ is the Day of Judgement. The perfect فَلَمْ تَجِدُوا is jussive after لَمْ, and the whole clause is the result of the إِذَا clause before it.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا أَعْرِفُ أَنَّ الْجُيُوشَ مُقِيمُونَ فِي مَكَانِهِمْ لِأَنَّكَ رَسَمْتَ لَهُمْ بِالْإِقَامَةِ ثَلٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ مَعَ أَنَّهُمْ فَقَدُوكَ فِي هَذِهِ الْمُدَّةِ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا مَا ذَا يَفْعَلُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā aʿrifu anna al-juyūsha muqīmūna fī makānihim li-annaka rasamta lahum bi-al-iqāmati thalāthata ayyāmin maʿa annahum faqadūka fī hādhihi al-muddati wa-lam yaʿlamū mā dhā yafʿalūna
sentences.l: And I, I know that the armies are staying in their place, because you decreed to them the staying three days, even though they have missed you in this period, and they did not know what they should do.
sentences.i: I know the armies are still waiting where they are, because you ordered them to stay three days, though they have lost you in the meantime and do not know what to do.
sentences.n: مُقِيمُونَ is nominative plural after أَنَّ الْجُيُوشَ, a Middle Arabic agreement (classical would have a feminine singular or the broken plural's own agreement); the edition prints it so. ثَلٰثَةَ is the defective ثلثة of the print, pointed with a dagger alif, and is accusative of duration. مَا ذَا is printed as two words, and we keep them apart; read it as "what".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ غَابَ سَاعَةً وَهُوَ مُتَفَكِّرٌ ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ قَبَّلَ يَدَ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ وَقَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Sharkānu hādhā al-kalāma ghāba sāʿatan wa-huwa mutafakkirun thumma innahu qabbala yada al-malikati Abrīzata wa-qāla
sentences.l: And when Sharkān heard this speech, he was absent an hour, and he pondering; then that he kissed the hand of the queen Abrīza, and said:
sentences.i: When Sharkān heard this, he fell silent for an hour, lost in thought. Then he kissed the hand of Queen Abrīza and said,
sentences.n: غَابَ سَاعَةً, "was absent for an hour", is the idiom for being lost in thought; the "hour" is just a while. ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ is the stock "then he" of narration.

sentences.t: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي مَنَّ عَلَّيَ بِكِ وَجَعَلَكِ سَبَبًا لِسَلَامَتِي وَسَلَامَةِ مَنْ مَعِي وَلَكِنْ يَعِزُّ عَلَّيَ فِرَانَكِ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ مَا يَجْرِي عَلَيْكِ بَعْدِي
sentences.tr: al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi alladhī manna ʿalayya bi-ki wa-jaʿalaki sababan li-salāmatī wa-salāmati man maʿī wa-lākin yaʿizzu ʿalayya firānaki wa-lā aʿlamu mā yajrī ʿalayki baʿdī
sentences.l: Praise be to God, who bestowed-favour upon me by you, and made you a cause for my safety and the safety of whoever is with me; but it is hard upon me, your separation, and I do not know what will run upon you after me.
sentences.i: Praise be to God, who showed me favour through you and made you the cause of my safety and the safety of all who are with me. But it grieves me to part from you, and I do not know what will befall you after I am gone.
sentences.n: The edition prints the shadda in عَلَّيَ on the lām instead of the yāʾ; we keep it where it is printed, and the word is the usual عَلَيَّ, "upon me". فِرَانَكِ is printed with a nūn and is surely فِرَاقَكِ, "your parting", with a misprinted letter. مَنَّ عَلَيَّ بِـ is "to confer a favour on me by (giving) ...", and يَعِزُّ عَلَيَّ means "it is hard on me".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ اذْهَبْ أَنْتَ الْآنَ إِلَى عَسْكَرِكَ وَرُدَّهُمْ وَإِنْ كَانَتِ الرُّسُلُ عِنْدَهُمْ فَاقْبِضْ عَلَيْهِمْ حَتَّى يَظْهَرَ لَكُمُ الْخَيْرُ وَأَنْتُمْ بِالْقُرْبِ مِنْ بِلَادِكُمْ وَبَعْدَ ثَلٰثَةِ أَيَّامٍ أَنَا أُلْحِقُكُمْ وَمَا تَدْخُلُونَ بَغْدَادًا إِلَّا وَكُلُّنَا سَوَاءٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu idhhab anta al-āna ilā ʿaskarika wa-ruddahum wa-in kānati al-rusulu ʿindahum fa-iqbiḍ ʿalayhim ḥattā yaẓhara lakumu al-khayru wa-antum bi-al-qurbi min bilādikum wa-baʿda thalāthati ayyāmin anā ulḥiqukum wa-mā tadkhulūna Baghdādan illā wa-kullunā sawāʾun
