sentences.l: And she said to him: Go, you, now to your army and turn them back; and if the messengers are with them, seize them, until the good appears to you, while you are near your lands; and after three days I, I will join you, and you will not enter Baghdad except while all-of-us are equal.
sentences.i: She said to him, "Go to your army now and bring them back. If the envoys are with them, seize them, until the way becomes clear for you while you are still close to your own country. In three days I will join you, and you will not enter Baghdad unless we all enter together."
sentences.n: وَكُلُّنَا سَوَاءٌ, literally "and all of us equal", is a circumstantial clause: they will enter Baghdad only together, no one ahead of the others. بَغْدَادًا is printed with an alif for the accusative tanwīn, and is so pointed even though the name is usually treated as diptote.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ لَمَّا أَرَادَ الِانْصِرَافَ قَالَتْ لَهُ وَالْعَهْدُ الَّذِي بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَكَ لَاتَنْسَاءُ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu lammā arāda al-inṣirāfa qālat lahu wa-al-ʿahdu alladhī baynī wa-baynaka lātansāʾu
sentences.l: Then that when he wished the departure, she said to him: And the covenant which is between me and between you, do not forget it.
sentences.i: Then, as he was about to leave, she said to him, "And do not forget the covenant between you and me."
sentences.n: لَاتَنْسَاءُ is printed as one word with a final hamza where we expect لَا تَنْسَاهُ, "do not forget it" (hamza and hāʾ look alike in the print); we point it as printed, but read it so. The pledge she means is the promise exchanged between them earlier. وَالْعَهْدُ, "the covenant", is put first for emphasis, with the pronoun left to the verb.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا نَهَضَتْ قَائِمَةً مَعَهُ لِأَجْلِ التَّوْدِيعِ وَالْعِنَاقِ وَإِطْفَاءِ نَارِ الْأَشْوَاقِ وَوَدَّعَتْهُ وَعَانَقَتْهُ وَبَكَتْ بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: thumma innahā nahaḍat qāʾimatan maʿahu li-ajli al-tawdīʿi wa-al-ʿināqi wa-iṭfāʾi nāri al-ashwāqi wa-waddaʿathu wa-ʿānaqathu wa-bakat bukāʾan shadīdan wa-anshadat taqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: Then that she rose standing with him, for the sake of the farewell and the embrace and the quenching of the fire of longings; and she bade him farewell and embraced him and wept a weeping, intense; and she recited, saying, poetry:
sentences.i: Then she rose and went with him to take her leave, to embrace him and quench the fire of longing. She said farewell to him and embraced him and wept bitterly, and she recited these verses:
sentences.n: نَهَضَتْ قَائِمَةً, "she rose up standing", is a pleonasm, an accusative of state that adds almost nothing. نَارِ الْأَشْوَاقِ, "the fire of longings", is a stock image for passion; the verses she recites come in the next section.

sentences.t:
وَدَّعْتُهَا وَيَدِى الْيَمِينُ لِادْمُعِي * وَيَدِى الْيَسَارُ لِضَمَّةٍ وَعِنَاقِ
قَالَتْ اَمَا تَخْشَى الْفَضِيحَةَ قُلْتُ لَا * يَوْمَ الْوَدَاعِ فَضِيحَةُ الْعُشَّاقِ
sentences.tr:
waddaʿtuhā wa-yadī al-yamīnu li-admuʿī * wa-yadī al-yasāru li-ḍammatin wa-ʿināqi
qālat amā takhshā al-faḍīḥata qultu lā * yawma al-wadāʿi faḍīḥatu al-ʿushshāqi
sentences.l:
I bade her farewell, my right hand for my tears, * and my left hand for an embrace and a clasp.
She said: Do you not fear the scandal? I said: No. * The day of farewell is the scandal of the lovers.
sentences.i: I said farewell to her, my right hand given to my tears and my left to an embrace and a clasp. She said, "Do you not fear disgrace?" I said, "No: the day of parting is the lovers' own day of disgrace."
sentences.n: The two verses are the lines she recites as she parts from him. The second line is compressed: "the day of farewell is the lovers' scandal" means that parting is the one time lovers may weep and cling in public without shame. The verse is copied as printed, marks and all (note the spelling يَدِى with ى, and the bare alif in لِادْمُعِي, which is لِأَدْمُعِي, "for my tears", with the hamza unwritten).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ فَارَقَهَا شَرْكَانُ وَنَزَلَ مِنَ الدَّيْرِ وَقَدَّمُوا لَهُ جَوَادَهُ فَرَكِبَ وَخَرَجَ طَالِبًا لِلْجِسْرِ فَوَصَلَ إِلَيْهِ وَمَرَّ مِنْ فَوْقِهِ وَدَخَلَ بَيْنَ تِلْكَ الْأَشْجَارِ
sentences.tr: thumma fāraqahā Sharkānu wa-nazala mina al-dayri wa-qaddamū lahu jawādahu fa-rakiba wa-kharaja ṭāliban li-al-jisri fa-waṣala ilayhi wa-marra min fawqihi wa-dakhala bayna tilka al-ashjāri
sentences.l: Then Sharkān parted from her, and went down from the monastery, and they brought-forward to him his steed, and he rode and went out, seeking the bridge; and he arrived at it, and passed over above it, and entered between those trees.
sentences.i: Then Sharkān took leave of her and came down from the monastery. His steed was brought forward, and he mounted and rode out, making for the bridge. He reached it, crossed over it, and entered among those trees.
sentences.n: وَقَدَّمُوا لَهُ جَوَادَهُ has a plural verb with no stated subject: "they brought him his horse", that is, the servants did, so English says "his steed was brought".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا تَخَلَّصَ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْأَشْجَارِ وَشَقَّ فِي ذَلِكَ الْمَرْجِ وَإِذَا هُوَ بِثَلَٰثَةِ فَوَارِسَ فَأَخَذَ لِنَفْسِهِ مِنْهُمُ الْحَذَرَ وَشَهَرَ سَيْفَهُ وَانْحَدَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā takhallaṣa min tilka al-ashjāri wa-shaqqa fī dhālika al-marji wa-idhā huwa bi-thalāthati fawārisa fa-akhadha li-nafsihi minhumu al-ḥadhara wa-shahara sayfahu wa-inḥadara
sentences.l: And when he got-free from those trees and clove through that meadow, then behold he was at three horsemen; and he took for himself from them the wariness, and drew his sword, and went down.
sentences.i: When he had come clear of those trees and was cutting across that meadow, behold, there were three horsemen before him. He took care on his own account against them, drew his sword, and rode down toward them.
sentences.n: ثَلٰثَةِ is printed ثلثة, without the long ā; we point it with the dagger alif so that it reads thalāthati. وَإِذَا هُوَ بِ is the "behold" construction: the بِ after إِذَا only marks what suddenly appears.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرُبُوا مِنْهُ وَنَظَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا عَرَفُوهُ وَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ فَإِذَا هُوَ أَحَدُهُمُ الْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَمَعَهُ أَمِيرَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qarubū minhu wa-naẓara baʿḍuhum baʿḍan ʿarafūhu wa-naẓara ilayhim fa-idhā huwa aḥaduhumu al-wazīru Dandānu wa-maʿahu amīrāni
sentences.l: And when they drew near from him, and some-of-them looked at others, they knew him; and he looked at them, and behold he was one-of-them, the vizier Dandān, and with him two emirs.
sentences.i: As they drew near him they looked at one another and recognised him, and he looked at them, and found that one of them was the vizier Dandān, with two emirs beside him.
sentences.n: نَظَرَ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا, literally "some of them looked at others", is the reciprocal idiom, "they looked at one another".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ وَعَرَفُوهُ تَرَجَّلُوا لَهُ وَسَلَّمُوا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾawhu wa-ʿarafūhu tarajjalū lahu wa-sallamū ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And when they saw him and knew him, they dismounted for him and greeted upon him.
sentences.i: When they saw him and knew him they dismounted in his honour and greeted him.

sentences.t: وَسَأَلَهُ الْوَزِيرُ عَنْ سَبَبِ غِيَابِهِ فَأَخْبَرَهُمْ عَنْ جَمِيعِ مَا جَرَى لَهُ مَعَ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ مِنْ أَوَّلِهِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ فَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-saʾalahu al-wazīru ʿan sababi ghiyābihi fa-akhbarahum ʿan jamīʿi mā jarā lahu maʿa al-malikati Abrīzata min awwalihi ilā ākhirihi fa-ḥamida Allāha taʿālā ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: And the vizier asked him about the cause of his absence, and he informed them about all that had happened to him with the queen Abrīza, from its beginning to its end; and he praised God, Exalted, for that.
sentences.i: The vizier asked him why he had been away, and he told them everything that had happened to him with Queen Abrīza, from beginning to end, and he praised God the Most High for it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ شَرْكَانُ ارْحَلُوا بِنَا مِنْ هَذِهِ الْبِلَادِ لِأَنَّ الرُّسُلَ الَّذِينَ جَاؤُا مَعَنَا رَحَلُوا مِنْ عِنْدِنَا لِيُعْلِمُوا مَلِكَهُمْ بِقُدُومِنَا فَرُبَّمَا أَسْرَعُوا إِلَيْنَا وَقَبَضُوا عَلَيْنَا
sentences.tr: thumma qāla Sharkānu irḥalū binā min hādhihi al-bilādi li-anna al-rusula alladhīna jāʾū maʿanā raḥalū min ʿindinā li-yuʿlimū malikahum bi-qudūminā fa-rubbamā asraʿū ilaynā wa-qabaḍū ʿalaynā
sentences.l: Then Sharkān said: Journey-off with us from this land, because the messengers who came with us have journeyed off from with us in order that they inform their king of our arrival, and perhaps they will hasten to us and seize upon us.
sentences.i: Then Sharkān said, "Let us leave this country, for the messengers who came with us have gone from us to tell their king that we are here, and they may well hurry after us and seize us."
sentences.n: جَاؤُا is printed جاوا, with no hamza; it is the ordinary jāʾū, "they came", spelled as it sounds, and the hamza is marked on the wāw. ارْحَلُوا بِنَا, literally "journey with us", means "let us all set out".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَادَى شَرْكَانُ فِي عَسْكَرِهِ بِالرَّحِيلِ فَرَحَلُوا كُلُّهُمْ وَلَا زَالُوا سَائِرِينَ مُجِدِّينَ فِي السَّيْرِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى سَطْحِ الْوَادِي
sentences.tr: thumma nādā Sharkānu fī ʿaskarihi bi-al-raḥīli fa-raḥalū kulluhum wa-lā zālū sāʾirīna mujiddīna fī al-sayri ilā an waṣalū ilā saṭḥi al-wādī
sentences.l: Then Sharkān called out in his army for the departure, and they all journeyed off, and they did not cease going, striving, in the going, until they arrived at the surface of the valley.
sentences.i: Then Sharkān proclaimed through his army the order to march, and they all set out, and kept on travelling at full effort until they reached the floor of the valley.
sentences.n: وَلَا زَالُوا is printed with a space, ولا زالوا, though it is the one verb lā zālū, "they did not cease", which with the participles that follow means "they kept on going". We keep the space as printed.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتِ الرُّسُلُ قَدْ تَوَجَّهُوا إِلَى مَلِكِهِمْ وَأَخْبَرُوهُ بِقُدُومِ شَرْكَانَ فَجَهَّزَ إِلَيْهِ عَسْكَرًا لِيَقْبِضُوا عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى مَنْ مَعَهُ هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الرُّسُلِ وَمَلِكِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-kānati al-rusulu qad tawajjahū ilā malikihim wa-akhbarūhu bi-qudūmi Sharkāna fa-jahhaza ilayhi ʿaskaran li-yaqbiḍū ʿalayhi wa-ʿalā man maʿahu hādhā mā kāna min amri al-rusuli wa-malikihim
sentences.l: And the messengers had gone-toward their king, and informed him of the arrival of Sharkān, and he equipped for him an army, that they seize upon him and upon whoever was with him. This is what was of the affair of the messengers and their king.
sentences.i: Meanwhile the messengers had gone to their king and told him that Sharkān was coming, and he had fitted out an army to seize him and all who were with him. So much for the messengers and their king.
sentences.n: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ … is the storyteller's stock formula for closing one strand of the tale before turning to another, as in the next unit.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ شَرْكَانَ وَوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ وَأَمِيرَيْنِ فَإِنَّهُمْ قَدْ أَشْرَفَ الْأَرْبَعَةُ عَلَى عَسْكَرِهِمْ وَصَاحُوا عَلَيْهِمُ ارْحَلُوا ارْحَلُوا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri Sharkāna wa-wazīri Dandāna wa-amīrayni fa-innahum qad ashrafa al-arbaʿatu ʿalā ʿaskarihim wa-ṣāḥū ʿalayhimu irḥalū irḥalū
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of Sharkān and the vizier-of Dandān and two emirs: indeed they, the four had overlooked their army, and they cried upon them: Journey off, journey off!
sentences.i: As for Sharkān, the vizier Dandān and the two emirs, the four of them came up to their army and shouted to them, "March! March!"
sentences.n: The grammar here is loose Middle Arabic. وَوَزِيرِ دَنْدَانَ is printed without the article ("the vizier-of Dandān") and وَأَمِيرَيْنِ without any "the" or "his"; فَإِنَّهُمْ "indeed they" is followed by a singular verb أَشْرَفَ whose subject is الْأَرْبَعَةُ "the four", which the pronoun anticipates. We point all of it as printed. أَشْرَفَ عَلَى is "to come to overlook, to come up to".

sentences.t: فَرَحَلُوا مِنْ سَاعَتِهِمْ وَسَارُوا أَوَّلَ يَوْمٍ وَثَانِيَ يَوْمٍ وَثَالِثَ يَوْمٍ وَلَازَالُوا سَائِرِينَ إِلَى خَمْسَةِ أَيَّامٍ وَنَزَلُوا فِي وَادٍ كَثِيرِ الْأَشْجَارِ وَاسْتَرَاحُوا فِيهِ مُدَّةً
sentences.tr: fa-raḥalū min sāʿatihim wa-sārū awwala yawmin wa-thāniya yawmin wa-thālitha yawmin wa-lāzālū sāʾirīna ilā khamsati ayyāmin wa-nazalū fī wādin kathīri al-ashjāri wa-istarāḥū fīhi muddatan
sentences.l: And they journeyed off from their hour, and went the first day and the second day and the third day, and did not cease going until five days, and alighted in a valley, many-of the trees, and rested in it a while.
sentences.i: They set out that very hour and travelled the first day, the second day and the third, and went on travelling for five days in all. Then they camped in a valley thick with trees and rested there for a while.
sentences.n: وَلَازَالُوا is printed as one word here, but with a space in the unit before; both are the same lā zālū, "they did not cease". مِنْ سَاعَتِهِمْ, literally "from their hour", is the idiom for "at once".

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ رَحَلُوا مِنْهُ وَمَازَالُوا سَائِرِينَ مُدَّةَ خَمْسَةٍ وَعِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا حَتَّى أَشْرَفُوا عَلَى أَوَائِلِ بِلَادِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika raḥalū minhu wa-mā zālū sāʾirīna muddata khamsatin wa-ʿishrīna yawman ḥattā ashrafū ʿalā awāʾili bilādihim
sentences.l: And after that they journeyed off from it, and did not cease going the period of five and twenty days, until they overlooked the firsts of their lands.
sentences.i: After that they left the valley and kept on travelling for twenty-five days, until they came in sight of the borders of their own country.
sentences.n: وَمَازَالُوا is printed as one word, ومازالوا, where the previous unit printed it split: the same lā zālū, "they did not cease" (here with mā, as in ما زال). أَوَائِلُ بِلَادِهِمْ, literally "the firsts of their lands", is the outskirts or first districts.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلُوا إِلَى هُنَاكَ أَمِنُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَنَزَلُوا لِأَخْذِ الرَّاحَةِ فَخَرَجَ إِلَيْهِمْ أَهْلُ تِلْكَ الْبِلَادِ بِالضِّيَافَاتِ وَعَلِيقِ الْبَهَائِمِ وَالْإِقَامَاتِ فَأَقَامُوا يَوْمَيْنِ وَرَحَلُوا طَالِبِينَ دِيَارَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣalū ilā hunāka aminū ʿalā anfusihim wa-nazalū li-akhdhi al-rāḥati fa-kharaja ilayhim ahlu tilka al-bilādi bi-al-ḍiyāfāti wa-ʿalīqi al-bahāʾimi wa-al-iqāmāti fa-aqāmū yawmayni wa-raḥalū ṭālibīna diyārahum
sentences.l: And when they arrived at there, they felt-safe upon themselves, and alighted for the taking of the rest, and the people of those lands went out to them with the hospitalities and the fodder-of the beasts and the lodgings; and they stayed two days and journeyed off, seeking their homes.
sentences.i: When they reached that place they felt safe, and halted to take their rest. The people of those lands came out to them with hospitality gifts, fodder for the animals and provisions for the stay. They stayed two days and then set off again for their homes.
sentences.n: أَمِنُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ means "they felt safe for their lives" (Form I of أمن, not آمَنُوا, "they believed"). الْإِقَامَات are the lodgings and board a host provides, here the arrangements for a stay.

sentences.t: وَتَأَخَّرَ شَرْكَانُ بَعْدَهُمْ فِي مِائَةِ فَارِسٍ وَأَمَّرَ الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ فَسَارَ وَمَعَهُ الْجَيْشُ
sentences.tr: wa-taʾakhkhara Sharkānu baʿdahum fī miʾati fārisin wa-ammara al-wazīra Dandāna fa-sāra wa-maʿahu al-jayshu
sentences.l: And Sharkān lagged behind them, with a hundred horsemen, and he made-commander the vizier Dandān, and he went on and with him the army.
sentences.i: Sharkān stayed behind them with a hundred horsemen. He put the vizier Dandān in command, and Dandān went on with the army.
sentences.n: The shadda on the م of وَأَمَّرَ is the edition's own (أَمَّرَ is "to appoint as commander"). It may stand for the simpler وَأَمَرَ "and he ordered", which would read "he ordered the vizier Dandān, and he went on"; either way the sense is that Dandān led the army ahead.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ بَعْدَ مَسِيرِهِمْ بِيَوْمٍ عَوَّلَ شَرْكَانُ عَلَى السَّفَرِ فَرَكِبَ وَرَكِبَتْ مِائَةُ فَارِسٍ وَسَارُوا مِقْدَارَ فَرْسَخَيْنِ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى مَحَلِّ مَضِيقٍ بَيْنَ جَبَلَيْنِ وَإِذَا أَمَامَهُمْ غَبْرَةٌ وَعَجَاجٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna baʿda masīrihim bi-yawmin ʿawwala Sharkānu ʿalā al-safari fa-rakiba wa-rakibat miʾatu fārisin wa-sārū miqdāra farsakhayni ḥattā waṣalū ilā maḥalli maḍīqin bayna jabalayni wa-idhā amāmahum ghabaratun wa-ʿajājun
sentences.l: And when it was after their going by a day, Sharkān resolved upon the travelling, and he rode, and a hundred horsemen rode, and they went the measure of two parasangs until they arrived at a place-of a narrow-pass between two mountains, and behold in front of them dust and swirling-dust.
sentences.i: When a day had passed after the army's departure, Sharkān made up his mind to travel. He mounted, and his hundred horsemen mounted with him, and they rode about two leagues until they came to a defile between two mountains, and there before them was a cloud of dust and swirling grit.
sentences.n: رَكِبَتْ مِائَةُ فَارِسٍ has a feminine singular verb, since a hundred is taken as a collective. فَرْسَخ, the parasang, is about three and a half miles, so "two leagues" is a fair English match. مَحَلِّ مَضِيقٍ: the print gives محل مضيق, which we read as "a place of narrowing", a defile; it could also be a place, narrow, with the adjective مُضَيَّق, but the sense is the same.

sentences.t: فَمَنَعُوا خُيُولَهُمْ مِنَ السَّيْرِ مِقْدَارَ سَاعَةٍ حَتَّى انْكَشَفَ الْغُبَارُ وَبَانَ مِنْ تَحْتِهِ مِائَةُ فَارِسٍ لُيُوثٌ عَوَابِسُ وَفِي الْحَدِيدِ وَالزَّرَدِ غَوَاطِسُ
sentences.tr: fa-manaʿū khuyūlahum mina al-sayri miqdāra sāʿatin ḥattā inkashafa al-ghubāru wa-bāna min taḥtihi miʾatu fārisin layūthun ʿawābisu wa-fī al-ḥadīdi wa-al-zaradi ghawāṭisu
sentences.l: And they held back their horses from the going the measure of an hour until the dust was uncovered, and there appeared from beneath it a hundred horsemen, lions, scowling, and in the iron and the mail, plunged.
sentences.i: They held their horses back from moving for about an hour, until the dust cleared and out of it appeared a hundred horsemen, grim-faced lions, sunk deep in iron and chain-mail.
sentences.n: The last two words rhyme, عَوَابِسُ and غَوَاطِسُ, a touch of sajʿ (rhymed prose). عَوَابِس is "scowling, grim" (said of lions and warriors); غَوَاطِس is "plunged in", that is, wholly encased in steel.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَنْ قَرُبُوا مِنْ شَرْكَانَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ صَاحُوا عَلَيْهِمْ وَقَالُوا وَحَقِّ يُوحَنَّا وَمَرْيَمَ نَحْنُ بَلَغْنَا مَا أَمَّلْنَاهُ وَنَحْنُ خَلْفَكُمْ مُجِدُّونَ السَّيْرَ لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا حَتَّى سَبَقْنَاكُمْ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā an qarubū min Sharkāna wa-man maʿahu ṣāḥū ʿalayhim wa-qālū wa-ḥaqqi Yūḥannā wa-Maryama naḥnu balaghnā mā ammalnāhu wa-naḥnu khalfakum mujiddūna al-sayra laylan wa-nahāran ḥattā sabaqnākum ilā hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: And when that they drew near from Sharkān and whoever was with him, they cried upon them and said: And by the truth-of John and Mary, we have reached what we hoped for, and we have been behind you, striving the going night and day, until we have outstripped you to this place.
sentences.i: When they came close to Sharkān and his men, they shouted at them, "By John and by Mary, we have got what we hoped for! We have been on your heels, riding hard by night and by day, until we overtook you and got ahead of you here."
sentences.n: The oath is by the Christian saints, John and Mary, so these are Christian (Rūm) knights, the king's men. فَلَمَّا أَنْ is a Middle Arabic form with a redundant أَنْ ("when that"). مُجِدُّونَ is printed with a shadda (مجدّون), from أَجَدَّ, "to be earnest, press on"; the noun after it, السَّيْرَ, is accusative, "pressing the going".

sentences.t: فَانْزِلُوا عَنْ خُيُولِكُمْ وَأَعْطُونَا أَسْلِحَتَكُمْ وَسَلِّمُوا لَنَا أَنْفُسَكُمْ حَتَّى نَجُودَ عَلَيْكُمْ بِأَرْوَاحِكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-nzilū ʿan khuyūlikum wa-aʿṭūnā asliḥatakum wa-sallimū lanā anfusakum ḥattā najūda ʿalaykum bi-arwāḥikum
sentences.l: So come down from your horses, and give us your weapons, and hand over to us your selves, so that we show-generosity upon you with your souls.
sentences.i: So get down from your horses, give us your weapons, and surrender yourselves to us, and then we shall be generous and spare your lives.
sentences.n: جَادَ عَلَيْهِ بِ is "to be generous to him with", so the speakers present the sparing of life as a gift. The tone is mocking.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ ذَلِكَ قَامَتْ عَيْنَاهُ فِي أُمِّ رَأْسِهِ وَاحْمَرَّتْ وَجْنَتَاهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Sharkānu dhālika qāmat ʿaynāhu fī ummi raʾsihi wa-aḥmarrat wajnatāhu
sentences.l: And when Sharkān heard that, his two eyes stood in the mother-of his head, and his two cheeks reddened.
sentences.i: When Sharkān heard that, his eyes rolled up into his head and his cheeks flamed red.
sentences.n: قَامَتْ عَيْنَاهُ فِي أُمِّ رَأْسِهِ, "his eyes stood in the mother of his head", is the idiom for eyes turning up in rage; أُمُّ الرَّأْسِ is the crown or brain-pan. The print spaces ام راسه as two words, as here.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لِمَ يَا كِلَابَ النَّصَارَى جَسَرْتُمْ وَجِئْتُمْ إِلَى بِلَادِنَا وَمَشَيْتُمْ فِي أَرْضِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lima yā kilāba al-naṣārā jasartum wa-jiʾtum ilā bilādinā wa-mashaytum fī arḍinā
sentences.l: And he said: Why, O dogs of the Christians, have you dared, and come to our lands, and walked in our earth
sentences.i: He said, "Why, you dogs of the Christians, have you dared to come into our country and walk about in our land,
sentences.n: The speaker is Sharkān, and his speech begins here. لِمَ is "why?" (li- + mā, with the alif dropped), and the sentence runs on into the next unit.

sentences.t: وَمَا كَفَاكُمْ ذَلِكَ حَتَّى أَنَّكُمْ تُخَاطِرُونَ بِأَنْفُسِكُمْ وَتُخَاطِبُونَ بِهَذَا الْخِطَابِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā kafākum dhālika ḥattā annakum tukhāṭirūna bi-anfusikum wa-tukhāṭibūna bi-hādhā al-khiṭābi
sentences.l: And that did not suffice you, until that you risk with your selves and address with this address
sentences.i: and was it not enough for you to stake your own lives, but you must also speak to me in such words?
sentences.n: خَاطَرَ بِنَفْسِهِ means "to risk oneself, to gamble one's life"; the bi- marks what is staked. The speech ends in the next unit, with the question أَظَنَنْتُمْ.

sentences.t: أَظَنَنْتُمْ أَنَّكُمْ تَخْلُصُونَ مِنْ أَيْدِينَا وَتَعُودُونَ إِلَى بِلَادِكُمْ
sentences.tr: a-ẓanantum annakum takhluṣūna min aydīnā wa-taʿūdūna ilā bilādikum
sentences.l: Did you think that you escape from our hands and return to your lands?
sentences.i: Did you think you would slip out of our hands and go home to your own lands?"
sentences.n: The opening أَ is the particle that asks a yes-or-no question; here it is glued to the verb. The two verbs after أَنَّ are printed in the plain indicative (تَخْلُصُونَ, تَعُودُونَ), where Classical grammar would have the subjunctive; we point them as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَاحَ عَلَى مِائَةِ فَارِسٍ الَّذِينَ مَعَهُ وَقَالَ لَهُمْ دُونَكُمْ وَهَؤُلَاءِ الْكِلَابَ فَإِنَّهُمْ فِي عَدَدِكُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣāḥa ʿalā miʾati fārisin al-ladhīna maʿahu wa-qāla lahum dūnakum wa-hāʾulāʾi al-kilāba fa-innahum fī ʿadadikum
sentences.l: Then he cried upon a hundred of horsemen, those who were with him, and said to them: Yours-to-hand, and these dogs, for they are in your number.
sentences.i: Then he called out to the hundred horsemen who were with him and said to them, "Here they are, these dogs; take them, for they are no more than you in number."
sentences.n: صَاحَ عَلَى is "to shout at" someone to rouse them. مِائَةَ فَارِسٍ is followed by الَّذِينَ, a plural, because the hundred are many men. دُونَكُمْ is a stock exclamation, literally "(there is) at your hand", which takes an object, "take these, seize them"; it recurs below in this night. فِي عَدَدِكُمْ means "equal to your number".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَلَّ سَيْفَهُ وَحَمَلَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَحَمَلَتْ مَعَهُ الْمِائَةُ فَارِسٍ فَاسْتَقْبَلَتْهُمُ الْإِفْرَنْجُ بِقُلُوبٍ أَقْوَى مِنَ الصَّخْرِ
sentences.tr: thumma salla sayfahu wa-ḥamala ʿalayhim wa-ḥamalat maʿahu al-miʾatu fārisin fa-istaqbalat-humu al-Ifranju bi-qulūbin aqwā mina al-ṣakhri
sentences.l: Then he drew his sword and carried upon them, and carried with him the hundred-horseman; and the Franks met them with hearts stronger than the rock.
sentences.i: Then he drew his sword and charged them, and the hundred horsemen charged with him, and the Franks met them with hearts harder than rock.
sentences.n: حَمَلَ عَلَى is "to charge at". The printed المائة فارس puts the definite article on the first word of a number-noun phrase ("the hundred-horseman"); this is not Classical, and we point it as printed. الْاِفْرَنْجُ, "the Franks", is a collective that takes a feminine singular verb. The shadda on سلّ is the edition's own.

sentences.t: وَاصْطَدَمَتِ الرِّجَالُ بِالرِّجَالِ وَوَقَعَتِ الْأَبْطَالُ فِى الْأَبْطَالِ وَالْتَحَمَ الْقِتَالُ وَاشْتَدَّ النِّزَالُ وَعَظُمَتِ الْأَهْوَالُ وَقَدْ بَطَلَ الْقِيلُ وَالْقَالُ
sentences.tr: wa-iṣṭadamati al-rijālu bi-al-rijāli wa-waqaʿati al-abṭālu fī al-abṭāli wa-iltaḥama al-qitālu wa-ishtadda al-nizālu wa-ʿaẓumati al-ahwālu wa-qad baṭala al-qīlu wa-al-qālu
sentences.l: And men collided with men, and heroes fell among heroes, and the fight was joined-fast, and the duel grew hard, and the terrors grew great, and now gone to nothing was the "it-is-said" and the "he-said".
sentences.i: Men crashed against men and champions fell upon champions; the fighting locked, the combat grew fierce, the terrors multiplied, and all talk and chatter came to an end.
sentences.n: The clauses rhyme in -āl (rijāl, abṭāl, qitāl, nizāl, ahwāl, qāl), a stretch of rhymed prose (sajʿ); the literal line keeps the clause order so you can hear where the rhyme falls. النِّزَالُ is combat at close quarters, often on foot. الْقِيلُ وَالْقَالُ, literally "the it-was-said and the he-said", is an idiom for idle talk and argument. The edition prints فى with a dotless final ى throughout; we keep it.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا فِى الْحَرْبِ وَالْكِفَاحِ وَالضَّرْبِ بِالصِّفَاحِ إِلَى أَنْ وَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالْاِعْتِكَارِ فَانْفَصَلُوا عَنْ بَعْضِهِمُ الْبَعْضِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū fī al-ḥarbi wa-al-kifāḥi wa-al-ḍarbi bi-al-ṣifāḥi ilā an wallā al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri fa-infaṣalū ʿan baʿḍihimu al-baʿḍi
sentences.l: And they did not cease in the war and the close-fighting and the striking with the broad-blades, until the day turned its back and the night came on with the thick-darkness; and they parted from one another (from some-of-them, the some).
sentences.i: They kept on in the battle, the hand-to-hand fighting and the clash of blades until the day withdrew and night came on in thick darkness; then they broke apart from one another.
sentences.n: لَمْ يَزَالُوا is printed with an alif after the waw; we point it as printed ("they did not cease"). الصِّفَاحُ are broad blades, plural of صَفِيحَة. وَلَّى النَّهَارُ, "the day turned its back", is the formula for evening falling. عَنْ بَعْضِهِمُ الْبَعْضِ, "from some of them, the some", is a pleonastic way of saying "from one another".

sentences.t: وَاجْتَمَعَ شَرْكَانُ بِأَصْحَابِهِ فَلَمْ يَجِدْ أَحَدًا انْصَدَمَ مِنْهُمْ غَيْرَ أَرْبَعَةِ أَنْفُسٍ بِجِرَاحَاتٍ حَصَلَتْ لَهُمْ لَكِنْ رَأَهَا سَالِمَةً
sentences.tr: wa-ijtamaʿa Sharkānu bi-aṣḥābihi fa-lam yajid aḥadan inṣadama minhum ghayra arbaʿati anfusin bi-jirāḥātin ḥaṣalat lahum lākin raʾāhā sālimatan
sentences.l: And Sharkān gathered with his companions, and found no one struck-down of them except four selves, with wounds that had come to them; but he saw them safe.
sentences.i: Sharkān rallied with his companions and found none of them badly hurt except four men who had taken wounds; but he saw that these were not serious.
sentences.n: أَنْفُسٍ, literally "selves", is the counted word for "persons". رَأَهَا سَالِمَةً is hard to be sure of: the "them" is most likely the wounds, which he judged not dangerous, and that is how we have read it. The edition prints رأها with the precomposed hamza, which we keep.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ شَرْكَانُ وَاللَّهِ عُمْرِي أَخُوضُ بَحْرَ الْحَرْبِ الْعَجَّاجَ وَأُقَاتِلُ الرِّجَالَ فَمَا لَقِيتُ أَصْبَرَ عَلَى الْجِلَادِ وَمُلَاقَاةِ الرِّجَالِ مِثْلَ هَؤُلَاءِ الْأَبْطَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum Sharkānu wa-Allāhi ʿumrī akhūḍu baḥra al-ḥarbi al-ʿajjāja wa-uqātilu al-rijāla fa-mā laqītu aṣbara ʿalā al-jilādi wa-mulāqāti al-rijāli mithla hāʾulāʾi al-abṭāli
sentences.l: And Sharkān said to them: By God, my life, I plunge into the sea of the war, the surging, and I fight the men; and I have not met one more patient upon the sword-fight and the meeting of men, the like of these heroes.
sentences.i: Sharkān said to them, "By God, all my life I have waded into the surging sea of war and fought men, and I have never met any more steadfast in the sword-fight and the meeting of men than these champions."
sentences.n: عُمْرِي, "my life", is read here as an adverb, "in all my life". If the print meant the oath لَعَمْرِي ("by my life") the sense would barely change. الْعَجَّاجَ, "surging, roaring", is read as describing the sea (بحر), not the war. أَصْبَرَ is the comparative, "more patient", and is the object of لَقِيتُ: "I have met no one more patient", with مِثْلَ هَؤُلَاءِ completing the comparison.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهُ اِعْلَمْ أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ أَنَّ فِيهِمْ فَارِسًا إِفْرَنْجِيًّا وَهُوَ الْمُقَدَّمُ عَلَيْهِمْ لَهُ شَجَاعَةٌ وَطَعَنَاتٌ نَافِذَاتٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahu iʿlam ayyuhā al-maliku anna fīhim fārisan ifranjiyyan wa-huwa al-muqaddamu ʿalayhim lahu shajāʿatun wa-ṭaʿanātun nāfidhātun
sentences.l: And they said to him: Know, O king, that among them is a horseman, a Frank, and he is the one set-forward over them; to him is bravery and thrusts, piercing.
sentences.i: They said to him, "Know, O king, that among them is a Frankish horseman who is their leader. He has courage and thrusts that pierce right through.
sentences.n: الْمُقَدَّمُ عَلَى is "the one placed in front of, put in command of", a leader. The last two words, طَعَنَاتٌ نَافِذَاتٌ, are "thrusts, piercing": a plural of a non-person takes the feminine plural adjective.

sentences.t: غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ وَاللَّهِ عَفَاعَنَّا كِبَارًا وَصِغَارًا وَكُلُّ مَنْ وَقَعَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ يَتَغَافَلُ عَنْهُ وَلَا يُقَاتِلُهُ فَوَاللَّهِ لَوْأَ رَادَ قَتْلَنَا لَقَتَلَنَا بِأَجْمَعِنَا
sentences.tr: ghayra annahu wa-Allāhi ʿafā ʿannā kibāran wa-ṣighāran wa-kullu man waqaʿa bayna yadayhi yataghāfalu ʿanhu wa-lā yuqātiluhu fa-wa-Allāhi law arāda qatlanā la-qatalanā bi-ajmaʿinā
sentences.l: Except that he, by God, pardoned us, great and small; and everyone who fell between his two hands, he feigns heedlessness of him and does not fight him. By God, if he had wished our killing, he would have killed us, with all-of-us.
sentences.i: But, by God, he spared us, old and young alike, and whoever falls into his hands he pretends not to notice and does not fight. By God, if he had wanted to kill us, he would have killed every one of us."
sentences.n: عَفَاعَنَّا is printed as one word (عفا عنا, ʿafā ʿannā, "he pardoned us"). The words لوا راد are split in the print: they stand for لَوْ أَرَادَ "if he had wished", with the alif of أَرَادَ printed at the end of the first piece. We keep the print's split. كِبَارًا وَصِغَارًا "big and small" is an accusative of state. بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ, "between his two hands", means "before him, in his power". بِأَجْمَعِنَا, "with all of us", is an emphatic "every one of us".

sentences.t: فَتَحَيَّرَ شَرْكَانُ لِمَارَأَى مِنْ فِعْلِهِ وَسَمِعَ عَنْهُ ذَلِكَ الْمَقَالَ وَ قَالَ فِي غَدَاةِ غَدٍ نَصْطَفُّ نُبَارِزُهُمْ فَهَا نَحْنُ مِائَةٌ وَهُمْ مِائَةٌ وَإِنَّا نَطْلُبُ وَ النَّصْرَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ رَبِّ السَّمَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-taḥayyara Sharkānu li-mā raʾā min fiʿlihi wa-samiʿa ʿanhu dhālika al-maqāla wa- qāla fī ghadāti ghadin naṣṭaffu nubārizuhum fa-hā naḥnu miʾatun wa-hum miʾatun wa-innā naṭlubu wa- al-naṣra ʿalayhim min rabbi al-samāʾi
sentences.l: And Sharkān was bewildered at what he saw of his doing, and heard from him that saying, and he said: In the morning of tomorrow we line up, we duel them; for here we are a hundred and they are a hundred, and we seek the victory over them from the Lord of the sky.
sentences.i: Sharkān was amazed at what he had seen the man do and what he had heard about him, and he said, "Tomorrow morning we shall line up and fight them man to man. Here we are a hundred, and they are a hundred, and we ask the Lord of Heaven for victory over them."
sentences.n: Two stray و's appear at the ends of printed lines, each cut off from the word it belongs to: وَ قَالَ ("and he said") and وَ النَّصْرَ ("and the victory"). We leave them split as printed. لِمَارَأَى is لِمَا رَأَى "at what he saw", printed as one word, with the edition's own precomposed hamza on رأى. غَدَاةُ غَدٍ is "the morning of tomorrow". نَصْطَفُّ نُبَارِزُهُمْ, "we line up, we duel them", has no "and" between the verbs. رَبُّ السَّمَاءِ is a common name for God.

sentences.t: وَبَاتُوا تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْاِتِّفَاقِ وَأَمَّا الْإِفْرَنْجُ فَإِنَّهُمُ اجْتَمَعُوا عِنْدَ مُقَدَّمِهِمْ وَقَالُوا لَهُ إِنَّنَا مَا بَلَغْنَا الْيَوْمَ فِي هَؤُلَاءِ أَرَبًا
sentences.tr: wa-bātū tilka al-layla ʿalā dhālika al-ittifāqi wa-ammā al-Ifranju fa-innahum ijtamaʿū ʿinda muqaddamihim wa-qālū lahu innanā mā balaghnā al-yawma fī hāʾulāʾi araban
sentences.l: And they spent that night upon that agreement. And as for the Franks, they gathered at their leader, and said to him: We have not reached today, in these, any aim.
sentences.i: They spent that night in agreement on this plan. As for the Franks, they gathered around their leader and said to him, "We got nowhere with these men today."
sentences.n: بَاتَ means to spend the night. أَمَّا ... فَـ is the "as for ... then" frame. أَرَبًا, "an aim, a purpose, a need", is the thing not reached; ما بلغنا ... أربا is thus "we achieved nothing". The print has the precomposed ؤ in هؤلاء here, which we keep.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ فِي غَدَاةِ غَدٍ نَصْطَفُّ وَنُبَارِزُهُمْ وَاحِدًا بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ فَبَاتُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْاِتِّفَاقِ وَتَحَارَسَ الْفَرِيقَانِ إِلَى أَنْ أَصْبَحَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِالصَّبَاحِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum fī ghadāti ghadin naṣṭaffu wa-nubārizuhum wāḥidan baʿda wāḥidin fa-bātū ʿalā dhālika al-ittifāqi wa-taḥārasa al-farīqāni ilā an aṣbaḥa Allāhu taʿālā bi-al-ṣabāḥi
sentences.l: And he said to them: In the morning of tomorrow we line up and duel them, one after one. And they spent the night on that agreement, and the two parties kept-watch-on-each-other until God, exalted, brought-to-morning with the morning.
sentences.i: He said to them, "Tomorrow morning we shall line up and fight them one at a time." So they spent the night on that plan, and the two camps kept watch on each other until God, exalted is He, brought on the morning with its light.
sentences.n: تَحَارَسَ is the reciprocal form: the two sides each posted guards. أَصْبَحَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِالصَّبَاحِ is an unusual phrase, "God brought the morning with the morning"; the usual idiom is simply أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ. We translate for the sense.

sentences.t: فَرَكِبَ الْمَلِكُ شَرْكَانُ وَرَكِبَتْ مَعَهُ الْمِائَةُ فَارِسٍ وَأَتَوْا إِلَى الْمَيْدَانِ كُلُّهُمْ فَوَجَدُوا الْإِفْرَنْجَ قَدِ اصْطَفُّوا لِلْقِتَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-rakiba al-maliku Sharkānu wa-rakibat maʿahu al-miʾatu fārisin wa-ataw ilā al-maydāni kulluhum fa-wajadū al-Ifranja qadi iṣṭaffū li-al-qitāli
sentences.l: And King Sharkān rode, and the hundred-horseman rode with him, and they came to the field, all of them, and found the Franks had lined up for the fight.
sentences.i: King Sharkān mounted, and the hundred horsemen mounted with him, and they all came to the field and found the Franks already drawn up for battle.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ لِأَصْحَابِهِ إِنَّ أَعْدَاءَنَا قَدْ عَزَمُوا عَلَى مَا كَانُوا فِيهِ فَدُونَكُمْ وَالْمُبَادَرَةَ إِلَيْهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Sharkānu li-aṣḥābihi inna aʿdāʾanā qad ʿazamū ʿalā mā kānū fīhi fa-dūnakum wa-al-mubādarata ilayhim
sentences.l: And Sharkān said to his companions: Truly our enemies have resolved upon what they were in; so yours-to-hand, and the hastening to them.
sentences.i: Sharkān said to his companions, "Our enemies are set on what they were about yesterday, so go to it, and make haste against them."
sentences.n: عَزَمَ عَلَى is "to resolve on"; مَا كَانُوا فِيهِ, "what they were in", is the fighting they were engaged in. فَدُونَكُمْ وَالْمُبَادَرَةَ is the same exclamation as above; here the object is "the hastening", that is, "hurry at them".

sentences.t: فَنَادَى مُنَادٍ مِنَ الْإِفْرَنْجِ لَايَكُونُ قِتَالُنَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ إِلَّامُنَاوَبَةً بِأَنْ يَبْرُزَ بَطَلٌ مِنْكُمْ إِلَى بَطَلٍ مِنَّا
sentences.tr: fa-nādā munādin mina al-Ifranji lā yakūnu qitālunā fī hādhā al-yawmi illā munāwabatan bi-an yabruza baṭalun minkum ilā baṭalin minnā
sentences.l: Then a caller called, from the Franks: Our fighting shall not be on this day except by turns, in that a hero come forth from you to a hero from us.
sentences.i: Then a herald from the Franks called out, "Today our fighting shall be by turns only: one champion of yours to come out against one champion of ours."
sentences.n: لايكون and الامناوبة are each printed as one word: لَا يَكُونُ ("it shall not be") and إِلَّا مُنَاوَبَةً ("except by turns"), and we point them as printed. مُنَاوَبَةً, from نَاوَبَ "to take turns", is an accusative of manner. بِأَنْ يَبْرُزَ spells out what the turn-taking means.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ بَرَزَ فَارِسٌ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ شَرْكَانَ وَسَاقَ بَيْنَ الصَّفَّيْنِ وَقَالَ هَلْ مِنْ مُبَارِزٍ هَلْ مِنْ مُنَاجِزٍ لَايَبْرُزُلِي الْيَوْمَ كَسْلَانُ وَلَا عَاجِزٌ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika baraza fārisun min aṣḥābi Sharkāna wa-sāqa bayna al-saffayni wa-qāla hal min mubārizin hal min munājizin lā yabruzu lī al-yawma kaslānu wa-lā ʿājizun
sentences.l: And at that, a horseman came forth from the companions of Sharkān, and drove between the two ranks, and said: Is there any duellist? Is there any fighter-to-the-finish? No idler comes forth to me today, nor any weakling.
sentences.i: At that, one of Sharkān's horsemen rode out between the two lines and cried, "Is there a challenger? Is there a man to fight it out to the end? No idler and no weakling is to come out against me today!"
sentences.n: هَلْ مِنْ مُبَارِزٍ, "is there any challenger?", uses مِنْ to give the sense of "any at all". لايبرزلي is printed as one word, لَا يَبْرُزُ لِي "let no one come forth to me". مُنَاجِزٌ is a fighter who presses a fight to its end. الصَّفَّيْنِ is the dual, "the two ranks".

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَتِمَّ كَلَامُهُ حَتَّى بَرَزَإِلَيْهِ فَارِسٌ مِنَ الْإِفْرَنْجِ غَرِيقٌ فِي سِلَاحِهِ وَقُمَاشِهِ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَهُوَ رَاكِبٌ عَلَى جَوَادٍ أَشْهَبَ وَذَلِكَ الْإِفْرَنْجِيُّ لَانَبَاتَ بِعَارِضَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yatimma kalāmuhu ḥattā barazā ilayhi fārisun mina al-Ifranji gharīqun fī silāḥihi wa-qumāshihi min dhahabin wa-huwa rākibun ʿalā jawādin ashhaba wa-dhālika al-Ifranjiyyu lā nabāta bi-ʿāriḍayhi
sentences.l: And his speech had not been completed until a horseman came forth to him, from the Franks, drowned in his weapons and his gear of gold, and he was riding upon a horse, grey; and that Frank, no growth on his two cheeks.
sentences.i: He had hardly finished speaking when a Frankish horseman rode out against him, buried in armour and gear of gold, mounted on a grey steed. This Frank had no beard on his cheeks.
sentences.n: برزاليه is printed as one word, بَرَزَ إِلَيْهِ "came forth to him"; لانبات is likewise لَا نَبَاتَ "no growth". غَرِيقٌ فِي سِلَاحِهِ, "drowned in his weapons", means "covered from head to foot in arms"; مِنْ ذَهَبٍ, "of gold", belongs to the gear. أَشْهَبُ is grey or white-grey. A youth with no beard on his عَارِضَانِ (the sides of the face) is very young.

sentences.t: فَسَاقَ جَوَادَهُ حَتَّى وَقَفَ فِى وَسَطِ الْمَيْدَانِ وَأَخَذَ مَعَهُ فِي الضَّرْبِ وَالطِّعَانِ فَلَمْ يَكُنْ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ حَتَّى طَعَنَهُ الْإِفْرَنْجِيُّ بِالرُّمْحِ فَنَكَسَهُ عَنْ جَوَادِهِ وَأَخَذَهُ أَسِيرًا وَقَادَهُ حَقِيرًا
sentences.tr: fa-sāqa jawādahu ḥattā waqafa fī wasaṭi al-maydāni wa-akhadha maʿahu fī al-ḍarbi wa-al-ṭiʿāni fa-lam yakun ghayra sāʿatin ḥattā ṭaʿanahu al-Ifranjiyyu bi-al-rumḥi fa-nakasahu ʿan jawādihi wa-akhadhahu asīran wa-qādahu ḥaqīran
sentences.l: And he drove his horse until he stopped in the middle of the field, and took up with him in the striking and the thrusting. It was not other than an hour until the Frank thrust him with the spear, and overturned him from his horse, and took him as a prisoner, and led him, abased.
sentences.i: He spurred his horse until he halted in the middle of the field and engaged him in blows and thrusts. It lasted no more than an hour before the Frank speared him, toppled him from his horse, took him prisoner and led him off in disgrace.
sentences.n: The subject of سَاقَ is the Frankish rider. أَخَذَ مَعَهُ فِي is "to set about with him in". فَلَمْ يَكُنْ غَيْرَ سَاعَةٍ, "it was nothing other than an hour", is a way to say "it took only an hour". نَكَسَهُ, "to turn upside down", is the word for tipping a man out of the saddle. حَقِيرًا is a state: "abased".

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ بِهِ قَوْمُهُ وَمَنَعُوهُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ إِلَى الْمَيْدَانِ وَأَخْرَجُوا غَيْرَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa bihi qawmuhu wa-manaʿūhu an yakhruja ilā al-maydāni wa-akhrajū ghayrahu
sentences.l: And his people rejoiced at him, and forbade him to go out to the field, and brought out another than him.
sentences.i: His people rejoiced over him and forbade him to go out to the field again, and sent out another man in his place.
sentences.n: فَرِحَ بِهِ is "to rejoice in or at him": the bi- marks the cause of joy. They kept their champion back, presumably to spare him, and sent another man out.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ خَرَجَ إِلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ آخَرُ وَهُوَأَخُ الْأَسِيرِ وَوَقَفَ مَعَهُ فِى الْمَيْدَانِ وَحَمَلَ الْاِثْنَانِ عَلَى بَعْضِهِمَا سَاعَةً يَسِيرَةً
sentences.tr: wa-qad kharaja ilayhi mina al-muslimīna ākharu wa-huwa akhu al-asīri wa-waqafa maʿahu fī al-maydāni wa-ḥamala al-ithnāni ʿalā baʿḍihimā sāʿatan yasīratan
sentences.l: And there had come out to him, from the Muslims, another, and he was the brother of the prisoner, and he stood with him in the field, and the two charged upon each other an hour, small.
sentences.i: Then another of the Muslims rode out to meet him, the brother of the captive, and took his stand with him in the field, and the two clashed for a short while.
sentences.n: وهواخ is printed as one word: وَهُوَ أَخُ, "and he was the brother of", with the final و of أَخُو left off in the spelling, so we point it أَخُ (read akhū). آخَرُ keeps the printed precomposed آ. سَاعَةً يَسِيرَةً is "a little while", literally "a light hour".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ كَرَّ الْإِفْرَنْجِيُّ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِ وَغَالَطَهُ وَطَعَنَهُ بِعَقِبِ الرُّمْحِ فَنَكَّسَهُ عَنْ جَوَادِهِ وَأَخَذَهُ أَسِيرًا
sentences.tr: thumma karra al-Ifranjiyyu ʿalā al-muslimi wa-ghālaṭahu wa-ṭaʿanahu bi-ʿaqibi al-rumḥi fa-nakkasahu ʿan jawādihi wa-akhadhahu asīran
sentences.l: Then the Frank wheeled upon the Muslim, and tricked him, and thrust him with the end of the spear, and overturned him from his horse, and took him as a prisoner.
sentences.i: Then the Frank wheeled on the Muslim, tricked him, struck him with the butt of his lance, toppled him from his horse and took him prisoner.
sentences.n: كَرَّ عَلَى is the war term for turning round to charge again. غَالَطَهُ is "he deceived him", presumably with a feint. عَقِبُ الرُّمْحِ is, we think, the butt end of the lance (literally "heel"), which may be what the Frank used so as not to kill his man; this is our reading, not certain. The shaddas on كرّ and نكّسه are the edition's own.

sentences.t: وَلَازَالَتِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمْ وَاحِدًا بَعْدَ وَاحِدٍ وَالْإِفْرَنْجِيُّ يَأْسِرُهُمْ إِلَى أَنْ وَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالْاِعْتِكَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā zālati al-muslimīna yakhruju minhum wāḥidan baʿda wāḥidin wa-al-Ifranjiyyu yaʾsiruhum ilā an wallā al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri
sentences.l: And did-not-cease the Muslims (one) comes out from them, one after one, and the Frank captures them, until the day turned its back and the night came on with the thick-darkness.
sentences.i: The Muslims kept coming out, one after another, and the Frank kept capturing them, until the day withdrew and night came on in thick darkness.
sentences.n: This is Middle Arabic. The print has لازالت as a single word, with feminine singular verb, followed by المسلمين in the oblique ending and a singular يخرج: roughly "the Muslims did not cease, each one coming out". We point exactly what is printed rather than repair it into Classical لَمْ يَزَلِ الْمُسْلِمُونَ يَخْرُجُونَ. Notice that lā zālat here means "did not cease" (Classical mā zālat); the same night-fall formula as above ends the unit.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَسَرُوا مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ عِشْرِينَ فَارِسًا فَلَمَّا عَايَنَ شَرْكَانُ ذَلِكَ عَظُمَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-qad asarū mina al-muslimīna ʿishrīna fārisan fa-lammā ʿāyana Sharkānu dhālika ʿaẓuma ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And indeed they had taken captive, of the Muslims, twenty horsemen; and when Sharkān beheld that, it grew-great upon him,
sentences.i: The Franks had also taken twenty Muslim horsemen captive, and when Sharkān saw this, it weighed heavily on him,
sentences.n: عَظُمَ عَلَيْهِ, literally "it grew great upon him", means that it was hard for him to bear.

sentences.t: وَجَمَعَ أَصْحَابَهُ وَقَالَ لَهُمْ مَا هَذَا الْأَمْرُ الَّذِي حَلَّ بِنَا
sentences.tr: wa-jamaʿa aṣḥābahu wa-qāla lahum mā hādhā al-amru alladhī ḥalla bi-nā
sentences.l: and he gathered his companions and said to them: What is this, the affair that has alighted upon us?
sentences.i: and called his companions together, and said to them, "What is this that has befallen us?"
sentences.n: حَلَّ بِـ, "to alight upon", is the usual verb for a misfortune that comes down on people.

sentences.t: أَنَا أَخْرُجُ فِي غَدَاةِ غَدٍ إِلَى الْمَيْدَانِ وَأَطْلُبُ بِرَازَ الْمُقَدَّمِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَنْظُرُ مَنْ كَانَ السَّبَبَ فِي دُخُولِهِ إِلَى بِلَادِنَا وَأُحَذِّرُهُ مِنْ قِتَالِنَا فَإِنْ أَبَى قَاتَلْنَاهُ وَإِنْ صَالَحَنَا صَالَحْنَاهُ
sentences.tr: anā akhruju fī ghadāti ghadin ilā al-maydāni wa-aṭlubu birāza al-muqaddami ʿalayhim wa-anẓuru man kāna al-sababa fī dukhūlihi ilā bilādinā wa-uḥadhdhiruhu min qitālinā fa-in abā qātalnāhu wa-in ṣālaḥanā ṣālaḥnāhu
sentences.l: I go out in the morning of tomorrow to the field, and seek the single-combat of the one-set-over them, and see who was the cause in his entering into our lands, and warn him off our fighting; and if he refuses, we fight him, and if he makes-peace with us, we make peace with him.
sentences.i: Tomorrow at dawn I will ride out to the field and challenge their commander to single combat. I will find out what brought him into our country, and warn him against fighting us. If he refuses, we will fight him; if he makes peace with us, we will make peace with him.
sentences.n: The present tense here is a firm resolve ("I go out" for "I shall go out"). بِرَاز is single combat, a man-to-man challenge before the armies. In the last two clauses the past tense after إِنْ (فَإِنْ أَبَى … وَإِنْ صَالَحَنَا) stands for the future: "if he refuses … if he makes peace".

sentences.t: وَبَاتُوا عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ إِلَى أَنْ أَصْبَحَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِالصَّبَاحِ فَرَكِبَتِ الطَّائِفَتَانِ وَاصْطَفَّتِ الْفَرِيقَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-bātū ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli ilā an aṣbaḥa Allāhu taʿālā bi-al-ṣabāḥi fa-rakibati al-ṭāʾifatāni wa-iṣṭaffati al-farīqāni
sentences.l: And they spent-the-night upon this state until God, Exalted, brought-the-morning with the morning; and the two parties mounted, and the two sides drew-up-in-ranks.
sentences.i: They passed the night in this state until God brought in the morning. Then the two armies mounted and drew up their ranks.
sentences.n: أَصْبَحَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى بِالصَّبَاحِ is a stock phrase, with God as the subject: He "brought the morning in with the dawn". The two dual nouns (الطَّائِفَتَانِ, الْفَرِيقَانِ) are the two armies, and the verbs after them are feminine singular, as is usual for collectives. هَذَا الْحَالِ treats حَال as masculine.

sentences.t: فَأَرَادَ شَرْكَانُ أَنْ يَخْرُجَ إِلَى الْمَيْدَانِ وَإِذَا بِالْإِفْرَنْجِ قَدْ تَرَجَّلَ مِنْهُمْ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ نِصْفِهِمْ قُدَّامَ فَارِسٍ مِنْهُمْ وَمَشَوْا فَدَانَهُ إِلَى أَنْ صَارُوا فِي وَسْطِ الْمَيْدَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-arāda Sharkānu an yakhruja ilā al-maydāni wa-idhā bi-al-Ifranji qad tarajjala minhum aktharu min niṣfihim quddāma fārisin minhum wa-mashaw fa-dānahu ilā an ṣārū fī wasṭi al-maydāni
sentences.l: And Sharkān wished to go out to the field, and behold! with the Franks: there had dismounted of them more than half of them before a horseman of them; and they walked, and fa-dānahu (obscure), until they were in the middle of the field.
sentences.i: Sharkān was about to ride out to the field when suddenly more than half of the Franks dismounted in front of one of their horsemen and walked on with him until they stood in the middle of the field.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِـ is the "behold!" of surprise; the بِـ only marks what appears. الْإِفْرَنْج are the Franks (European Christians). The word فَدَانَهُ is obscure. As printed it reads "and he drew near him", but the plural مَشَوْا before it expects a plural verb, so it may be a slip for something like فَدَنَوْا ("and they drew near"). We point it as printed and translate the sense of the whole.

sentences.t: فَتَأَمَّلَ شَرْكَانُ ذَلِكَ الْفَارِسَ وَإِذَا بِالْفَارِسِ الْمُقَدَّمِ عَلَيْهِمْ لَابِسٌ قَبَاءً أَزْرَقَ مِنْ أَطْلَسٍ وَوَجْهُهُ فِيهِ كَالْبَدْرِ إِذَا أَشْرَقَ
sentences.tr: fa-taʾammala Sharkānu dhālika al-fārisa wa-idhā bi-al-fārisi al-muqaddami ʿalayhim lābisun qabāʾan azraqa min aṭlasin wa-wajhuhu fīhi ka-al-badri idhā ashraqa
sentences.l: And Sharkān scrutinised that horseman, and behold! the horseman, the one-set-over them, [was] wearing a blue coat, of satin, and his face, in it, like the full moon when it shines.
sentences.i: Sharkān studied that horseman. The commander of the Franks was dressed in a blue satin coat, and his face shone like the full moon when it rises.
sentences.n: The printed أ in تَأَمَّلَ is kept as in the edition. لَابِسٌ is the predicate after "behold", so it stands in the nominative. The قَبَاء is a long coat, and أَطْلَس is satin. فِيهِ ("in it") after وَجْهُهُ is awkward and may be a slip; we point it as printed and leave it out of the idiomatic line.

sentences.t: وَمِنْ فَوْقِهِ زَرَدِيَّةٌ ضَيِّقَةُ الْعُيُونِ وَبِيَدِهِ سَيْفٌ مُهَنَّدٌوَ هُوَ رَاكِبٌ عَلَى جَوَادٍ أَدْهَمَ فِي وَجْهِهِ غُرَّةٌ كَالدِّرْهَمِ
sentences.tr: wa-min fawqihi zaradiyyatun ḍayyiqatu al-ʿuyūni wa-bi-yadihi sayfun muhannadun-wa huwa rākibun ʿalā jawādin adhama fī wajhihi ghurratun ka-al-dirhami
sentences.l: and above it a coat-of-mail, narrow-of the-eyes; and in his hand a sword, Indian-tempered, and he riding upon a steed, black, in its face a blaze like the dirham.
sentences.i: Over it he wore a close-meshed coat of mail, and in his hand was a tempered Indian blade. He rode a black charger with a blaze on its brow as round as a dirham.
sentences.n: زَرَدِيَّة is a coat of mail, and ضَيِّقَةُ الْعُيُونِ, "narrow of eyes", means that its rings are small and closely linked. مُهَنَّد is a sword of Indian steel. The edition prints the و of "and he" joined to the end of مُهَنَّدٌ, and we keep it that way: read مُهَنَّدٌ وَهُوَ. أَدْهَم is a black horse, and the غُرَّة is the white blaze on its forehead; the face in question is the horse's.

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ الْإِفْرَنْجِيُّ لَانَبَاتَ بِعَارِضَيْهِ وَلَكَزَ جَوَادَهُ حَتَّى صَارَ فِي وَسْطِ الْمَيْدَانِ وَأَشَارَ إِلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ وَهُوَ يَقُولُ بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ فَصِيحٍ
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika al-Ifranjiyyu lānabāta biʿāriḍayhi wa-lakaza jawādahu ḥattā ṣāra fī wasṭi al-maydāni wa-ashāra ilā al-muslimīna wa-huwa yaqūlu bi-lisānin ʿarabiyyin faṣīḥin
sentences.l: And that Frank, no-growth on his two cheeks, and he prodded his steed until he was in the middle of the field, and signalled to the Muslims, he saying in a tongue, Arabic, eloquent:
sentences.i: That Frank had no down on his cheeks. He spurred his horse until he stood in the middle of the field, motioned to the Muslims, and called out in clear, eloquent Arabic:
sentences.n: لَانَبَاتَ is printed as one word, لا نبات, "no growth": the Frank is beardless, a youth. عَارِضَان are the cheeks. لَكَزَ is to jab a horse with heel or fist to urge it forward.

sentences.t: يَا شَرْكَانُ يَا ابْنَ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ يَا مَنْ مَلَكَ الْحُصُونَ وَأَخْرَبَ الْبُلْدَانَ دُونَكَ وَالْحَرْبَ وَالْقِتَالَ وَابْرُزَّ إِلَى مَنْ قَدْ نَاصَفَكَ فِي الْمَيْدَانِ فَأَنْتَ سَيِّدُ قَوْمِكَ وَأَنَا سَيِّدُ قَوْمِي
sentences.tr: yā Sharkānu yā ibna ʿUmara ibni al-Nuʿmāni yā man malaka al-ḥuṣūna wa-akhraba al-buldāna dūnaka wa-al-ḥarba wa-al-qitāla wa-ibruzza ilā man qad nāṣafaka fī al-maydāni fa-anta sayyidu qawmika wa-anā sayyidu qawmī
sentences.l: O Sharkān, O son of ʿUmar son of al-Nuʿmān, O you who possessed the fortresses and laid waste the lands: have-at-you the war and the fighting, and come-forth to one who has met-you-half-way in the field; for you are lord of your people and I am lord of my people,
sentences.i: "Sharkān, son of ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, you who have taken fortresses and laid lands waste, here is war and battle for you! Come out against one who is your equal on this field. You are the lord of your people, and I am the lord of mine,
sentences.n: دُونَكَ followed by an accusative works as a command, "have at it, take it". The shadda on وَابْرُزَّ is printed; the imperative needs none, so it may be emphatic or a slip. نَاصَفَ comes from نِصْف, "half", so مَنْ نَاصَفَكَ is one who meets you on equal terms. The speech goes on in the next unit.

sentences.t: فَمَنْ غَلَبَ مِنَّا صَاحِبَهُ قَامَتْ قَوْمُهُ تَحْتَ طَاعَتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-man ghalaba minnā ṣāḥibahu qāmat qawmuhu taḥta ṭāʿatihi
sentences.l: so whoever of us overcomes his companion, his people stand under his obedience.
sentences.i: and whichever of us beats the other, the beaten man's people shall come under the winner's rule."
sentences.n: The two "his" in the Arabic are ambiguous. The sense must be that the loser's people come under the winner's obedience, and the idiomatic line says so. قَوْم takes a feminine verb here (قَامَتْ) as a collective noun.

sentences.t: فَمَا اسْتَتَمَّ كَلَامَهُ حَتَّى بَرَزَلَهُ شَرْكَانُ وَقَلْبُهُ مِنَ الْغَيْظِ مَلَّانُ وَسَاقَ جَوَادَهُ حَتَّى دَنَا مِنَ الْإِفْرَنْجِيِّ فِي الْمَيْدَانِ وَطَبَّقَ عَلَيْهِ كَالْأَسَدِ الْغَضْبَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā istatamma kalāmahu ḥattā barazalahu Sharkānu wa-qalbuhu mina al-ghayẓi mallānu wa-sāqa jawādahu ḥattā danā mina al-Ifranjiyyi fī al-maydāni wa-ṭabbaqa ʿalayhi ka-al-asadi al-ghaḍbāni
sentences.l: And he had not completed his speech when Sharkān came-forth-to-him, his heart, from the rage, full; and he drove his steed until he drew near the Frank in the field, and closed upon him like the lion, the enraged.
sentences.i: He had scarcely finished speaking when Sharkān rode out against him, his heart brimming with rage. He urged his horse on until he came close to the Frank in the field, and fell upon him like an angry lion.
sentences.n: فَمَا … حَتَّى means "hardly had he … when". بَرَزَلَهُ is printed as one word, برز له, "came out to him". مَلَّان is printed with a shadda; the usual word for "full" is مَلْآن, so we point the printed form as it stands. The endings -ān in مَلَّان, الْمَيْدَان and الْغَضْبَان give the passage a rhyme. طَبَّقَ عَلَيْهِ is to close upon, cover or swoop on someone.

sentences.t: فَتَلَقَّى الْإِفْرَنْجِيَّ فِي الْمَيْدَانِ بِخِبْرَةٍ وَإِمْكَانٍ وَصَدَمَهُ صَدْمَةَ الْفُرْسَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-talaqqā al-Ifranjiyya fī al-maydāni bi-khibratin wa-imkānin wa-ṣadamahu ṣadmata al-fursāni
sentences.l: And he met the Frank in the field with skill and ability, and collided-with him the collision of the horsemen.
sentences.i: He met the Frank in the field with skill and strength, and struck him as cavalrymen strike.
sentences.n: The subject is Sharkān and the Frank is the object, so the Frank takes the accusative. The -ān rhyme (الْمَيْدَان … إِمْكَان … الْفُرْسَان) carries on from the last sentence. صَدْمَةَ الْفُرْسَانِ is an accusative of manner, "the clash of horsemen".

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَا فِي الطَّعْنِ وَالضَّرْبِ وَلَمْ يَزَالَا فِى كَرٍّوَ فَرٍّوَ أَخْذٍ وَرَدٍّ كَأَنَّهُمَا جَبَلَانِ اصْطَدَمَا أَوْ بَحْرَانِ الْتَطَمَا
sentences.tr: wa-akhadhā fī al-ṭaʿni wa-al-ḍarbi wa-lam yazālā fī karrin-wa farrin-wa akhdhin wa-raddin ka-annahumā jabalāni iṣṭadamā aw baḥrāni iltaṭamā
sentences.l: And the two began in the thrusting and the striking, and did not cease in attack-and retreat-and taking and giving-back, as though the two were two mountains that clashed, or two seas that crashed together.
sentences.i: The two fell to thrusting and striking, and went on without pause, charging and retreating, giving blows and taking them, like two mountains colliding or two seas dashing together.
sentences.n: The edition prints the و ("and") joined to كَرّ and to فَرّ, so the words read كَرّ وَفَرّ, "attack and retreat", and then أَخْذ وَرَدّ, "taking and giving back"; we keep the printed spacing. أَخَذَ فِي means "to begin, set about". The verbs ending -ā are duals for the two fighters. التَطَمَ is said of waves crashing together.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالَا فِى قِتَالٍ إِلَى أَنْ وَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالْاِعْتِكَارِ وَانْفَصَلَ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمَا مِنْ صَاحِبِهِ وَعَادَ إِلَى قَوْمِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālā fī qitālin ilā an wallā al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri wa-infaṣala kullun minhumā min ṣāḥibihi wa-ʿāda ilā qawmihi
sentences.l: And the two did not cease in fighting until the day turned-away and the night came-on with the darkness, and each of the two parted from his companion and returned to his people.
sentences.i: They fought on until the day turned away and night came on in thick darkness; then each broke off from the other and went back to his own people.
sentences.n: الِاعْتِكَار is the piling up of darkness, thick gloom. The print spells فِى with ى here, as in the last sentence; we keep it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اجْتَمَعَ شَرْكَانُ بِأَصْحَابِهِ قَالَ لَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ijtamaʿa Sharkānu bi-aṣḥābihi qāla lahum
sentences.l: And when Sharkān assembled with his companions, he said to them:
sentences.i: When Sharkān was back among his companions, he said to them,
sentences.n: اجْتَمَعَ بِـ is "to meet with, be together with".

sentences.t: مَا رَأَيْتُ مِثْلَ هَذَا الْفَارِسِ قَطُّ إِلَّا أَنِّي رَأَيْتُ مِنْهُ خَصْلَةً لَمْ أَرَهَا مِنْ أَحَلٍ غَيْرِهِ وَهُوَا نَّهُ إِذَا لَاحَ لَهُ فِي خَصْمِهِ مَضْرِبٌ قَاتِلٌ يُقَلِّبُ الرُّمْحَ وَيَضْرِبُهُ بِعَقِبِهِ وَلَكِنْ مَا أَدْرِي مَاذَا يَكُونُ مِنِّي وَمِنْهُ وَمُرَادِي أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي عَسْكَرِنَا مِثْلُهُ وَمِثْلُ أَصْحَابِهِ
sentences.tr: mā raʾaytu mithla hādhā al-fārisi qaṭṭu illā annī raʾaytu minhu khaṣlatan lam arahā min aḥalin ghayrihi wa-huwā nnahu idhā lāḥa lahu fī khaṣmihi maḍribun qātilun yuqallibu al-rumḥa wa-yaḍribuhu bi-ʿaqibihi wa-lākin mā adrī mādhā yakūnu minnī wa-minhu wa-murādī an yakūna fī ʿaskarinā mithluhu wa-mithlu aṣḥābihi
sentences.l: Not I-saw the like of this horseman ever, except that I saw from him a trait I have not seen from anyone-else other-than-him; and it-is that-he, when there shows to him in his adversary a striking-place, deadly, he turns-over the lance and strikes with the butt-end of it. But I do not know what will be from me and from him; and my aim is that there be in our army the like of him and the like of his companions.
sentences.i: "I have never seen the like of this knight, except that I noticed in him one habit I have seen in no other man: whenever a mortal opening shows itself in his opponent, he turns his lance over and strikes with the butt. But I cannot tell what will come of him and me. My wish is that our army had men like him and his companions."
sentences.n: This is Sharkān speaking, to his own men, about the Frankish champion he has been fighting. The edition prints مِنْ أَحَلٍ غَيْرِهِ, which makes no sense; the ل is surely a slip for د, giving مِنْ أَحَدٍ غَيْرِهِ, "from anyone other than him", and the translation follows that. We point the word as printed. Also printed: وَهُوَا نَّهُ, split after the و-alif, for وَهُوَ أَنَّهُ "and it is that"; we keep the printer's split (the stray alif ends the first word, and the أَ of أَنَّهُ is lost at the start of the second).

sentences.t: وَبَاتَ شَرْكَانُ فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ خَرَجَ لَهُ الْإِفْرَنْجِيُّ وَنَزَلَ فِي وَسَطِ الْمَيْدَانِ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَيْهِ شَرْكَانُ
sentences.tr: wa-bāta Sharkānu fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu kharaja lahu al-Ifranjiyyu wa-nazala fī wasaṭi al-maydāni wa-aqbala ʿalayhi Sharkānu
sentences.l: And Sharkān spent-the-night; and when the morning became-morning, there went out to him the Frank, and he came down in the middle of the field, and Sharkān advanced upon him.
sentences.i: Sharkān passed the night, and when morning came the Frank rode out to meet him and took his place in the middle of the field, and Sharkān came on against him.
sentences.n: الْإِفْرَنْجِيُّ, "the Frank" (from Ifranj, the Franks, that is western Europeans), is the narrator's name for the disguised queen while she is taken for a knight. بَاتَ is "to spend the night", so the first clause just says that Sharkān slept.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَخَذَا فِى الْقِتَالِ وَأَوْسَعَا فِى الْحَرْبِ وَالْمَجَالِ وَامْتَدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمَا الْأَعْنَاقُ وَلَمْ يَزَالَا فِي حَرْبٍ وَكِفَاحٍ وَطَعْنٍ بِالرِّمَاحِ إِلَى أَنْ وَلَّى النَّهَارُ وَأَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ بِالِاعْتِكَارِ
sentences.tr: thumma akhadhā fī al-qitāli wa-awsaʿā fī al-ḥarbi wa-al-majāli wa-imtaddat ilayhimā al-aʿnāqu wa-lam yazālā fī ḥarbin wa-kifāḥin wa-ṭaʿnin bi-al-rimāḥi ilā an wallā al-nahāru wa-aqbala al-laylu bi-al-iʿtikāri
sentences.l: Then the two took to the fighting, and gave-wide-scope in the war and the field-of-play, and there stretched toward the two of them the necks; and they did not cease in war and combat and thrusting with the lances, until the day turned-away and the night came-on with the thick-gathering-of-darkness.
sentences.i: Then the two of them fell to fighting and held nothing back in battle and manoeuvre. Necks stretched toward them from every side, and they never ceased from war, hand-to-hand struggle and thrusting with lances, until the day turned away and night came on in thickening dusk.
sentences.n: أَخَذَا فِي is the usual "began to", with the verb in the dual for the two fighters. امْتَدَّتْ إِلَيْهِمَا الْأَعْنَاقُ, "the necks stretched toward them", describes the onlookers craning to watch. Note the rhymes (sajʿ) الْقِتَالِ / الْمَجَالِ and كِفَاحٍ / الرِّمَاحِ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ افْتَرَقَا وَرَجَعَا إِلَى قَوْمِهِمَا وَصَارَ كُلٌّ مِنْهُمَا يَحْكِي لِأَصْحَابِهِ مَا لَاقَاهُ مِنْ صَاحِبِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma iftaraqā wa-rajaʿā ilā qawmihimā wa-ṣāra kullun minhumā yaḥkī li-aṣḥābihi mā lāqāhu min ṣāḥibihi
sentences.l: Then the two parted and returned to their people, and each one of the two became relating to his companions what he had met from his fellow.
sentences.i: Then they parted and went back to their own people, and each began telling his companions what he had met with from the other.
sentences.n: صَارَ with a present verb, "became relating", means "began to relate".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْإِفْرَنْجِيَّ قَالَ لِأَصْحَابِهِ فِي غَدٍ يَكُونُ الِانْفِصَالُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-Ifranjiyya qāla li-aṣḥābihi fī ghadin yakūnu al-infiṣālu
sentences.l: Then that the Frank said to his companions: In tomorrow will be the separation.
sentences.i: Then the Frank said to his companions, "Tomorrow it will be decided."
sentences.n: الِانْفِصَالُ is a parting, a severing; here the settling of the contest.

sentences.t: وَبَاتُوا تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ إِلَى الصَّبَاحِ ثُمَّ رَكِبَ الِاثْنَانِ وَحَمَلَا عَلَى بَعْضِهِمَا وَلَمْ يَزَالَا فِى الْحَرْبِ إِلَى نِصْفِ النَّهَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-bātū tilka al-laylata ilā al-ṣabāḥi thumma rakiba al-ithnāni wa-ḥamalā ʿalā baʿḍihimā wa-lam yazālā fī al-ḥarbi ilā niṣfi al-nahāri
sentences.l: And they spent-the-night that night until the morning; then the two mounted, and charged upon each-other, and did not cease in the war until the half of the day.
sentences.i: They spent that night till morning. Then the two mounted and charged at one another, and kept up the fight until midday.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ عَمِلَ الْإِفْرَنْجِيُّ حِيلَةً وَلَكَزَ الْجَوَادَ ثُمَّ جَذَّ بِهِ بِاللِّجَامِ فَعَثَرَ بِهِ وَرَمَاهُ فَانْكَبَّ عَلَيْهِ شَرْكَانُ وَأَرَادَ أَنْ يَضْرِبَهُ بِالسَّيْفِ خَوْفًا أَنْ يَطُولَ بِهِ الْمِطَالُ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika ʿamila al-Ifranjiyyu ḥīlatan wa-lakaza al-jawāda thumma jadhdha bihi bi-al-lijāmi fa-ʿathara bihi wa-ramāhu fa-inkabba ʿalayhi Sharkānu wa-arāda an yaḍribahu bi-al-sayfi khawfan an yaṭūla bihi al-miṭālu
sentences.l: And after that the Frank made a ruse, and jabbed the steed, then pulled with it by the bridle, and it stumbled with him and threw him; and Sharkān fell-upon him, and wanted to strike him with the sword, in fear that the delay would be long with him.
sentences.i: After that the Frank played a trick. He jabbed his horse and hauled on the bridle, so that it stumbled and threw him. Sharkān bore down on him and meant to strike him with the sword, for fear the business would drag on.
sentences.n: The printed جَذَّ ("he cut") is odd with بِهِ; it may be a short writing of جَذَبَ, "he pulled" (جَذَبَ بِهِ, "he tugged it"), and we translate it so, pointing the word as printed. The fall is the Frank's own stratagem, as the next sentences show: the "knight" wants Sharkān to hear a woman's voice. خَوْفًا أَنْ يَطُولَ بِهِ الْمِطَالُ is literally "fearing that the delay might lengthen for him", that is, that the fight might be prolonged.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَ بِهِ الْإِفْرَنْجِيُّ وَقَالَ يَا شَرْكَانُ مَا هَكَذَا تَكُونُ الْفُرْسَانُ إِنَّمَا هَذَا فِعْلُ الْمَغْلُوبِ بِالنِّسْوَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥa bihi al-Ifranjiyyu wa-qāla yā Sharkānu mā hākadhā takūnu al-fursānu innamā hādhā fiʿlu al-maghlūbi bi-al-niswāni
sentences.l: And the Frank cried out at him, and said: O Sharkān, not thus are the horsemen; only this is the deed of the vanquished-one with the women.
sentences.i: The Frank shouted at him, "Sharkān, this is not how true horsemen behave! This is the deed of a beaten man dealing with women."
sentences.n: The reproach is double: a true knight does not strike a man who has fallen, and the speaker's own voice has just given away that "he" is a woman. بِالنِّسْوَانِ, "with the women", is compact; we take it as "in dealing with women".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْفَارِسِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ رَفَعَ طَرْفَهُ إِلَيْهِ وَأَمْعَنَ النَّظَرَ فِيهِ فَوَجَدَهُ الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِيزَةَ الَّتِي وَقَعَ لَهُ مَعَهَا مَا وَقَعَ فِى الدَّيْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Sharkānu min dhālika al-fārisi hādhā al-kalāma rafaʿa ṭarfahu ilayhi wa-amʿana al-naẓara fīhi fa-wajadahu al-malikata Abrīzata allatī waqaʿa lahu maʿahā mā waqaʿa fī al-dayri
sentences.l: And when Sharkān heard from that horseman this speech, he raised his eye to him and pressed-on the looking at him, and he found him the queen Abrīza, she-who there befell to him with her what befell, in the monastery.
sentences.i: When Sharkān heard these words from the knight, he raised his eyes to him and looked hard, and found that it was Queen Abrīza, the woman with whom he had had that adventure in the monastery.
sentences.n: وَجَدَهُ الْمَلِكَةَ takes two accusatives, "he found him (to be) the queen". أَمْعَنَ النَّظَرَ is "to look intently". الَّتِي وَقَعَ لَهُ مَعَهَا مَا وَقَعَ is a coy way of saying "the one with whom there happened to him what happened"; it recalls an earlier episode.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَرَفَهَا رَمَى السَّيْفَ مِنْ يَدِهِ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا مَا حَمَلَكِ عَلَى هَذِهِ الْفِعَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿarafahā ramā al-sayfa min yadihi wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhā wa-qāla lahā mā ḥamalaki ʿalā hādhihi al-fiʿāli
sentences.l: And when he knew her, he threw the sword from his hand, and kissed the earth between her two hands, and said to her: What carried you upon these deeds?
sentences.i: When he recognised her, he flung the sword from his hand, kissed the ground before her, and said, "What possessed you to do this?"
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا, "between her two hands", means "in front of her", the standard phrase of deference. هَذِهِ الْفِعَالِ pairs a feminine singular demonstrative with a plural noun, as Arabic often does with plurals of things.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ أَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَخْتَبِرَكَ فِى الْمَيْدَانِ وَأَنْظُرَ ثَبَاتَكَ فِي الْحَرْبِ وَالطِّعَانِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ الَّذِينَ مَعِي كُلُّهُمْ جَوَارِيَّ وَكُلُّهُنَّ بَنَاتُ أَبْكَارٍ
sentences.tr: qālat lahu aradtu an akhtabiraka fī al-maydāni wa-anẓura thabātaka fī al-ḥarbi wa-al-ṭiʿāni wa-hāʾulāʾi alladhīna maʿī kulluhum jawāriyya wa-kulluhunna banātu abkārin
sentences.l: She said to him: I wished to test you in the field and to look at your steadfastness in war and thrusting; and these who are with me, all-of-them [are] my girls, and all-of-them [fem.] daughters-of virgins.
sentences.i: She said to him, "I wanted to try you out on the field and see how you hold firm in battle and combat. These who are with me are all my maids, and every one of them is a virgin."
sentences.n: كُلُّهُمْ (masculine) and then كُلُّهُنَّ (feminine) both refer to the same girls: the masculine plural is the looser, Middle Arabic habit. جَوَارِيَّ has the printed shadda on the ي, which is simply the "my" ending joined to the plural. بَنَاتُ أَبْكَارٍ, literally "daughters of virgins", is the idiom for girls who are virgins.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ قَهَرْنَ فُرْسَانَكَ فِي حَوْمَةِ الْمَيْدَانِ وَلَوْلَا أَنَّ جَوَادِي قَدْ عَثَرَ بِي لَكُنْتَ تَرَى قُوَّتِي وَجِلَادِي
sentences.tr: wa-qad qahharna fursānaka fī ḥawmati al-maydāni wa-lawlā anna jawādī qad ʿathara bī lakunta tarā quwwatī wa-jilādī
sentences.l: And they have overpowered your horsemen in the thick of the field; and had it not been that my steed had stumbled with me, you would have been seeing my strength and my hardness.
sentences.i: They have already overpowered your horsemen in the thick of the field. And had my horse not stumbled under me, you would have seen my strength and my toughness.
sentences.n: لَكُنْتَ تَرَى, "you would have been seeing", is the ordinary way to give the result clause after لَوْلَا. Her claim that the horse really stumbled sits oddly with the narrator's account of a ruse, which is part of her playfulness.

sentences.t: فَتَبَسَّمَ شَرْكَانُ مِنْ قَوْلِهَا وَقَالَ لَهَا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى السَّلَامَةِ وَعَلَى اجْتِمَاعِي بِكِ يَا مَلِكَةَ الرُّمَّانِ
sentences.tr: fa-tabassama Sharkānu min qawlihā wa-qāla lahā al-ḥamdu li-Allāhi ʿalā al-salāmati wa-ʿalā ijtimāʿī biki yā malikata al-rummāni
sentences.l: And Sharkān smiled at her saying, and said to her: The praise [is] to God for the safety, and for my meeting with you, O queen of the pomegranate.
sentences.i: Sharkān smiled at her words and said, "Praise be to God for your safety, and for my meeting you again, O queen of the age."
sentences.n: The edition prints الرُّمَّانِ, "the pomegranate", which cannot be meant: the stock address is يَا مَلِكَةَ الزَّمَانِ, "O queen of the age", and الرمان is a slip for الزمان. We point the word as printed and let the idiomatic line give the sense. الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ عَلَى السَّلَامَةِ is what one says to someone who has come through a danger unharmed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِيزَةَ صَاحَتْ عَلَى جَوَارِيهَا وَأَمَرَتْهُنَّ أَنْ يَرَجَّلْنَ بَعْدَ أَنْ يُطْلِقْنَ الْعِشْرِينَ أَسِيرًا الَّذِينَ كُنَّ أَسَرْنَهُمْ مِنْ قَوْمِ شَرْكَانَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malikata Abrīzata ṣāḥat ʿalā jawārīhā wa-amarathunna an yarajjalna baʿda an yuṭliqna al-ʿishrīna asīran alladhīna kunna asarnahum min qawmi Sharkāna
sentences.l: Then that the queen Abrīza cried out at her girls, and commanded them that they dismount, after they release the twenty prisoners, those whom they had taken-captive from the people of Sharkān.
sentences.i: Then Queen Abrīza called to her maids and ordered them to dismount, once they had set free the twenty prisoners they had taken from Sharkān's men.
sentences.n: يَرَجَّلْنَ is printed with the shadda on the ج, the mark of the fifth form تَرَجَّلَ, "to dismount" (as فَتَرَجَّلُوا below); the first ت of يَتَرَجَّلْنَ seems to have dropped out. We point it as printed. Notice the pluperfect كُنَّ أَسَرْنَهُمْ, "they (f.) had captured them", with the feminine plural all through: the captors are the girls.

sentences.t: فَامْتَثَلَتِ الْجَوَارِي أَمْرَهَا ثُمَّ إِنَّهُنَّ قَبَّلْنَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِمَا فَقَالَ لَهُنَّ مِثْلُكُنَّ مَنْ يَكُنَّ عِنْدَ الْمُلُوكِ مُدَّخَرًا لِلشَّدَائِدِ
sentences.tr: fa-imtathalati al-jawārī amrahā thumma innahunna qabbalna al-arḍa bayna yadayhimā fa-qāla lahunna mithlukunna man yakunna ʿinda al-mulūki muddakharan li-al-shadāʾidi
sentences.l: And the girls complied-with her command; then that they kissed the earth between the two hands of the two of them; and he said to them: The like of you are those-who are with the kings a laid-up-thing for the hardships.
sentences.i: The maids carried out her command, then kissed the ground before the two of them, and Sharkān said to them, "Women like you are just the ones kings keep by them, stored up against hard times."
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِمَا is dual, "before the two of them", Abrīza and Sharkān. In مِثْلُكُنَّ مَنْ يَكُنَّ the plural feminine verb follows مَنْ by sense, while مُدَّخَرًا is masculine singular: Middle Arabic is relaxed about such agreement. For الشَّدَائِدِ the edition itself prints the ئ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَشَارَ إِلَى أَصْحَابِهِ أَنْ سَلِّمُوا عَلَيْهَا فَتَرَجَّلُوا جَمِيعًا وَقَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَىِ الْمَلِكَةِ أَبْرِيزَةَ وَقَدْ عَرَفُوا الْقَضِيَّةَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu ashāra ilā aṣḥābihi an sallimū ʿalayhā fa-tarajjalū jamīʿan wa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayi al-malikati Abrīzata wa-qad ʿarafū al-qaḍiyyata
sentences.l: Then that he signalled to his companions: that, Greet her; and they dismounted, all, and kissed the earth between the two hands of the queen Abrīza, they having known the matter.
sentences.i: Then he signalled to his companions to greet her, and they all dismounted and kissed the ground before Queen Abrīza, for by now they knew the whole affair.
sentences.n: أَنْ سَلِّمُوا عَلَيْهَا uses أَنْ to introduce the content of the signal, "that: greet her", an explanatory أَنْ which is followed by an imperative. The edition prints يدى with a final ى for يَدَيِ, "the two hands of".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَكِبَ مِانَتَا فَارِسٍ وَسَارُوا فِى اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ إِلَى مُدَّةِ سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: thumma rakiba miʾatā fārisin wa-sārū fī al-layli wa-al-nahāri ilā muddati sittati ayyāmin
sentences.l: Then rode two-hundred of horseman, and they travelled in the night and the day to a period of six days.
sentences.i: Then two hundred horsemen mounted, and they rode night and day for six days.
sentences.n: The edition prints مانتا, with ن where the word needs a hamza-seat: مِائَتَا فَارِسٍ, "two hundred horsemen" (literally "two hundred of horseman"). We point it for that reading. The verb رَكِبَ is singular before its plural subject, as Classical Arabic prefers when the verb comes first.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أَقْبَلُوا عَلَى الدِّيَارِ فَأَمَرَ شَرْكَانُ الْمَلِكَةَ أَبْرِيزَةَ وَجَوَارِيَهَا أَنْ يَتْزِعْنَ مَا عَلَيْهِنَّ مِنْ لِبَاسِ الْإِفْرَنْجِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika aqbalū ʿalā al-diyāri fa-amara Sharkānu al-malikata Abrīzata wa-jawārīhā an yatziʿna mā ʿalayhinna min libāsi al-Ifranji
sentences.l: And after that they came-on upon the abodes; and Sharkān commanded the queen Abrīza and her girls that they take-off what was upon them from the clothing of the Franks.
sentences.i: After that they came in sight of the inhabited country, and Sharkān told Queen Abrīza and her maids to take off the Frankish dress they were wearing.
sentences.n: يَتْزِعْنَ is printed so, with the ز before the ع and the ن last; it must be a slip (a transposition) for يَنْزِعْنَ, "they (f.) take off", and we translate it so, pointing the letters as printed. الدِّيَارِ, "the dwellings", is the settled land, that is, Sharkān's own territory.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahra Zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The edition prints the name as two words, شهر زاد; we keep the printed split. This is the formula that ends each night: dawn catches Shahrazād in mid-story and she breaks off.
